article.articleHeadline: Число случаев заболевания Эболой в Конго превысило 11 000
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The number of Ebola virus disease cases in Congo exceeded 11,000.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has reached 11,042 confirmed cases and 5,387 deaths, according to government data cited by Reuters. The outbreak has affected eight of the country’s 26 provinces, with many deaths occurring outside health facilities. North Kivu province accounts for nearly 40% of all new cases, and authorities warn that transmission in the northeastern region has escalated, with the spread described as out of control by Doctors Without Borders (MSF) on October 8. The report highlights ongoing challenges in surveillance, case management, and access to care in affected areas, underscoring geographic spread and a substantial fatality burden. These data reflect continuing Ebola activity in the DRC and have implications for regional public health responses.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ出血熱症例数が11,000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: 致死率が高く(5,387/11,042)8州に拡大、MSFが「制御不能」と警告しており、公衆衛生上深刻かつ国際的拡大リスクが認められる。
triage.notes: MSFが「制御不能」と表現し、医療施設外での死亡が多いことから、サーベイランス・症例管理体制の脆弱性が示唆される。続報でのRRA実施を推奨。

article.articleHeadline: Varian Baru Covid-19 PJ.2.1 Muncul di Singapura, Ini Gejala dan Faktanya
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: New COVID-19 variant PJ.2.1 has emerged in Singapore; here are its symptoms and the facts.
article.articleSummary: PJ.2.1, a recombinant SARS-CoV-2 variant, is drawing global attention after detection in multiple regions. It was first identified in Ontario, Canada, in May 2026 and has since spread to the United States, Israel, France, Spain, Australia, and New Zealand, with Asia reporting cases in Singapore, near Indonesia. Classified as a recombinant variant, PJ.2.1 derives from MC.10.1.7 within the JN.1 lineage that circulated through May 2025. It carries a spike protein with extensive mutations, marked by enhanced binding to the ACE2 receptor rather than marked antibody escape. No distinct symptom profile has emerged; manifestations align with common COVID-19 symptoms per WHO: fever, cough, sore throat, runny nose, headache, myalgia/arthralgia, fatigue, and in some cases dyspnea, GI symptoms, or anosmia. Ongoing mutation is anticipated; officials warn to monitor health updates, especially given proximity to Indonesia, and no specific case counts are provided.

triage.headline_ja: 新型コロナウイルスの新変異株PJ.2.1がシンガポールで出現、症状と事実について
triage.triage_reason: 新規組換え変異株PJ.2.1が複数国で検出され拡大しているが、重症度増加や症例数の具体的データはなく、インドネシアでの確認例もないため情報不足として経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 記事はインドネシア近隣のシンガポールでの変異株検出を報じているが、インドネシア国内での症例確認は明記されていないため、対象国リストに該当する発生国はなしと判断した。

diseases.name: Human Infection with Avian Influenza A H5N1

article.articleHeadline: EXPLAINER: How do bird flu, ASF threaten livestock?
article.articleSummary: Bird flu (avian influenza) and African swine fever (ASF) threaten the Philippines’ poultry and hog sectors. The Department of Agriculture monitors spread; WOAH notes avian influenza is classified as low- or highly pathogenic, spreading by direct contact, respiratory droplets and contaminated environments. As of Oct 16, bird flu affected 13 provinces across 10 regions. The DA banned poultry imports from Minnesota after confirmed H5N1 outbreaks in seven counties; a 2016 agreement would trigger a statewide ban if three or more counties were affected. Imports bans on Germany and Peru were lifted after they were declared free of HPAI. ASF is highly contagious among domestic and wild pigs, with up to 100% mortality, and has active cases in 236 barangays as of Oct 22; no human health risk. Vaccines from South Korea and the United States may gain regulatory approval in H1 2027. Culling and movement restrictions drive economic losses across farmers, traders and processors.

triage.headline_ja: 解説：鳥インフルエンザとアフリカ豚熱（ASF）は家畜にどのような脅威をもたらすか
triage.triage_reason: フィリピン国内で鳥インフルエンザ（H5N1含む）とASFが複数州・地域に拡大しており、経済的影響と社会的関心（農家・流通業者への打撃、政府機関の監視対応）が確認されるため、WPRO基準とSPC（社会的関心）の双方を満たしフルRRAへの移行が妥当と判断。
triage.notes: 本記事はフィリピンの家畜（鶏・豚）における鳥インフルエンザおよびASFの現況を解説する記事であり、ヒトへの感染事例は報告されていない（ASFについては『人への健康リスクなし』と明記）。ミネソタ州・韓国・ドイツ・ペルーは輸入禁止措置やワクチン開発に関する言及のみで、発生地域はフィリピンに限定される。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola Outbreak In Congo Tops 11,000 Cases
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has surpassed 11,000 cases, with 11,042 infections and 5,387 deaths, making it the country’s deadliest outbreak. The Bundibugyo ebolavirus responsible has no vaccine or proven treatment, and it has spread to eight of the DRC’s 26 provinces. Declared in mid-May, the outbreak has been hampered by ongoing conflict and a crippled health system, limiting containment efforts. The latest data come from Bunia, with health authorities reporting rapid transmission and a case fatality rate approaching 50%. There is no mention of imported or exported cases or new therapies in this update. The data reflect ongoing transmission despite regional response efforts.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ流行、感染者数が11,000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: 致死率約50%、ワクチン・治療法未確立のエボラ(ブンディブギョ株)が8州に拡大し、紛争により封じ込めが困難なため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する重大シグナル。
triage.notes: ワクチンや有効な治療法がないブンディブギョ株による流行で、紛争により保健システムが機能不全に陥っている点が懸念材料。致死率約50%は極めて高い。

article.articleHeadline: Congo's Ebola outbreak tops 11,000 cases as disease keeps spreading
article.articleSummary: As of Wednesday, Congo's Ebola outbreak has 11,042 infections and 5,387 deaths, according to health ministry data. The Bundibugyo virus driving the outbreak has no known vaccine or treatment and has spread to eight of Congo's 26 provinces, with activity centered in Bunia. Declared mid-May, this is the country’s deadliest Ebola outbreak, and containment has been hampered by ongoing conflict and a health-system crisis. The latest figures underscore sustained transmission in a fragile health landscape where therapeutic options are extremely limited and health services are strained. The report links continued spread to security challenges and systemic weaknesses, highlighting the absence of a vaccine or treatment for Bundibugyo virus as a core driver of the ongoing outbreak.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ出血熱アウトブレイク、感染者数1万1000人を突破し拡大継続
triage.triage_reason: 致死率の高いエボラ（ブンディブギョ株）がコンゴ8州に拡大し、ワクチン・治療法がなく、紛争下で封じ込めが困難なため国際的拡大リスクと公衆衛生への深刻な影響が認められる。
triage.notes: ブンディブギョ型エボラウイルスはワクチン・治療薬が未確立であり、紛争地域での対応が極めて困難。感染者数・死亡者数ともに過去最大規模の国内アウトブレイクとされ、継続的な監視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Cúm mùa tăng mạnh, ngành y tế khuyến cáo phòng bệnh
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Seasonal flu on the rise; health sector urges preventive measures.
article.articleSummary: Influenza season has risen in Ha Tinh Province, Vietnam, with 6,194 influenza-like illness cases recorded Jan–29 Oct 2026. October spiked to 902 cases, up 763 from September (~6.4-fold). In the first half, monthly counts ranged 611–937; July 172; August 197; September 139. The surge aligns with seasonal transition and fluctuating temperatures, with crowded indoor settings and poor ventilation increasing transmission risk in schools, offices, and public spaces. Common symptoms include fever, cough, sore throat, runny nose, headache, muscle pain, and fatigue. High-risk groups: children under 5, adults over 65, pregnant women, within 2 weeks post-partum, and those with chronic diseases or immunosuppression. Preventive measures: vaccination, mask use in health facilities and crowded places, hand hygiene, cough etiquette, ventilation, and seeking care if symptoms persist or worsen. Health authorities stress surveillance; experts warn flu raises risks of heart attack and stroke in the elderly. As of 11 November 2026.

triage.headline_ja: 季節性インフルエンザが急増、保健当局が予防を呼びかけ
triage.triage_reason: ベトナム・ハティン省で季節性インフルエンザ様疾患が急増しているが、重症度や異常性を示す情報はなく、典型的な季節性流行と考えられるため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 季節性インフルエンザの通常の増加であり、重症度や死亡率に関する具体的データは不明。地域内の学校・職場などでの感染拡大リスクが指摘されているが、現時点で国際的な懸念材料はない。

article.articleHeadline: RD Congo supera barrera de 11.000 casos de ébola, con 5.387 muertos
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: DR Congo surpasses 11,000 Ebola cases, with 5,387 deaths.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 11,000 confirmed cases, with 5,387 deaths as of November 9, 2026, per the National Institute of Public Health (INSP). Total infections reach 11,042 and the case fatality rate is 48.8%. Declared May 15, the outbreak is the second-largest and deadliest in history, after the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic that infected over 28,600 and caused more than 11,000 deaths. Eight of the DRC’s 26 provinces are affected, with many fatalities occurring outside treatment centers. Factors driving spread include delayed detection, ongoing conflict, and overwhelmed health services. The disease has now spread across East, Central, and West Africa, marking the broadest geographic extent of Ebola on the continent to date.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国、エボラ出血熱患者数が11,000人を突破、死者5,387人
triage.triage_reason: 致死率48.8%の大規模エボラ流行がDRC複数州に拡大し、史上2番目の規模となっており、国際的拡大・公衆衛生への深刻な影響が明確なためフルRRAへ移行すべき。
triage.notes: 記事はDRCにおけるエボラ流行の拡大を主題としており、史上2番目の規模の流行と報告。紛争・医療体制の逼迫により制御が困難な状況。モザンビーク・アンゴラは発生地域に含まれるが対象国リストに無く、記事本文でもDRC以外の国での発生は明記されていないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: CHDC Congo ghi nhận hơn 11.000 ca mắc Ebola
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: DR Congo records more than 11,000 Ebola cases.
article.articleSummary: Democratic Republic of Congo reports 11,042 Ebola cases and 5,387 deaths in the current outbreak, the most severe in years, with transmission spreading to eight of its 26 provinces. The outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo Ebola virus, for which there is no approved vaccine or specific therapy. The World Health Organization has, since May, declared Ebola outbreaks in both the Democratic Republic of Congo and neighboring Uganda as a Public Health Emergency of International Concern, underscoring international concern and the need for coordinated response. As of 11 November 2026, the outbreak remains ongoing with rising caseload and fatalities across affected regions.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国、エボラ感染者1万1千人以上を記録
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4項目すべてに該当する大規模エボラ流行であり、WHOがPHEICを宣言済みであることから即時フルRRAへ移行すべき案件。
triage.notes: ウガンダも発生地域として記載されPHEIC宣言対象だが、ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations から除外。致死率(約49%)が極めて高く、ワクチン・治療法未承認のブンディブギョ株による流行である点に留意。

article.articleHeadline: Еболата в ДР Конго надхвърли 11 000 потвърдени случая
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in DR Congo surpassed 11,000 confirmed cases
article.articleSummary: Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo has surpassed 11,000 confirmed cases, with 11,042 infections and 5,387 deaths since the outbreak was declared in mid-May. The outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo strain, now the second-largest in history by cases and deaths after the West Africa 2014–2016 epidemic (over 28,600 cases and more than 11,000 deaths). Eight of the DRC's 26 provinces are affected, led by Ituri and North Kivu, with spread to distant provinces. A high proportion of deaths have occurred outside health facilities. Factors worsening transmission include delayed detection, ongoing armed conflict, and overwhelmed health services. There are no approved vaccines or treatments for Bundibugyo; control relies on early case finding, isolation, contact tracing, supportive care by symptoms, and safe burials. The outbreak has crossed borders, underscoring the need for cross-border surveillance and information sharing, with WHO and African authorities providing support.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国でのエボラ出血熱、確認症例数が11,000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準3項目（深刻な公衆衛生影響、異常性、国境を越えた拡大）に該当し、WPRO基準も複数該当する大規模かつ深刻なエボラ流行であるため、フルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: Bundibugyo株による史上2番目の規模の流行で、死者5,387人、感染11,042人。武装紛争や保健システムの逼迫、承認済みワクチン・治療薬の不在が対応を困難にしている。Angolaが発生地域に含まれるが記事本文中に具体的言及がなく、対象国リストにも含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。

article.articleHeadline: تفشي إيبولا في الكونغو الديمقراطية يثير المخاوف... - الوكيل الإخباري
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo raises concerns...
article.articleSummary: As of 11 November 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo reports 11,042 laboratory-confirmed Ebola infections and 5,387 deaths in the current outbreak that began in mid-May. The outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo ebolavirus, a rare strain for which no approved vaccine or therapy exists. This is the second-largest and most deadly Ebola surge to date, surpassed only by the West Africa epidemic of 2014–2016, which infected more than 28,000 people and killed over 11,000. The outbreak has spread across eight of the DRC’s 26 provinces, with cases detected in multiple areas of the eastern, central, and western regions. Authorities warn that delayed case detection, ongoing conflict, and strained health services could accelerate transmission and complicate containment.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ出血熱が流行、懸念広がる
triage.triage_reason: DRCで11,042例・死亡5,387例という大規模かつ致死率の高いエボラ流行（稀なブンディブギョ株、ワクチン・治療薬なし）が8州に拡大しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルRRAへ進むべき。
triage.notes: Bluedotの発生地域にAngolaが含まれているが、記事サマリーではDRC国内の8州拡大のみ言及されており、Angolaでの発生は確認されないため除外した。史上2番目の規模・致死数のエボラ流行であり、紛争地域での対応困難、稀な株（Bundibugyo）でワクチン・治療薬が存在しない点が重大なリスク要因。

article.articleHeadline: RD Congo supera barrera de los 11.000 casos de ébola, incluidos 5.387 muertos
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: DR Congo surpasses 11,000 Ebola cases, including 5,387 deaths.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, declared May 15, has surpassed 11,000 confirmed cases with 5,387 deaths as of November 9, 2026, according to the National Institute of Public Health (INSP). Total infections reach 11,042 with a case fatality rate of 48.8%. It is the second-largest and deadliest Ebola outbreak in Africa, behind the 2014–2016 West Africa outbreak (over 28,600 infections and more than 11,000 deaths). Eight of 26 provinces are affected, and many deaths occur outside treatment centers. Late detection, conflict, and overwhelmed health systems have fueled faster spread. The outbreak has reached East, Central, and West Africa, marking the widest geographic expansion of Ebola on the continent to date.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国、エボラ症例1万1000件を突破、死者5387人
triage.triage_reason: 致死率48.8%の大規模エボラアウトブレイクが8州に拡大し、アフリカ史上2番目の規模となっており、国際的拡大・公衆衛生への深刻な影響が明白なためフルRRAへ進むべき。
triage.notes: 発生地域にMozambique、Angolaが含まれているが、記事サマリーではDRCのみが主題であり、他国への拡大は明記されていないため除外。'widest geographic expansion'はDRC国内の東・中央・西部地域への拡大を指すと解釈。

article.articleHeadline: Бројот потврдени случаи на ебола во Конго надмина 11 илјади, досега починати 5.387 лица
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The number of confirmed Ebola cases in Congo exceeded 11,000; so far 5,387 people have died.
article.articleSummary: As of 11 November 2026, the Democratic Republic of Congo reports 11,042 confirmed Ebola cases and 5,387 deaths, according to government data. The outbreak is driven by the Bundibugyo variant of Ebola virus, for which there is no approved effective therapy or vaccine. It is the second-largest Ebola epidemic in history, after West Africa (2014–2016), which recorded about 28,600 cases and more than 11,000 deaths. The disease has been confirmed in eight of 26 provinces, with a large share of fatalities occurring outside health facilities. Delayed case detection, armed conflict, and an overburdened health system fuel rapid spread. The outbreak now spans Eastern, Central, and Western Africa, constituting the widest geographic distribution of Ebola on the African continent to date.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでのエボラ確認症例数が1万1000人を超え、これまでに5,387人が死亡
triage.triage_reason: DRCでエボラ（ブンディブギョ株）の大規模流行が進行中で、致死率が高く、ワクチン・治療法が未確立かつ地理的拡大が顕著なため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: 記事はDRC単独での流行拡大に焦点を当てており、Angolaは発生地域リストに含まれるが記事本文では言及されていないため除外。史上2番目に大きいエボラ流行とされ、致死率も高く、医療体制の脆弱性・武力紛争が流行拡大の要因として挙げられている。

article.articleHeadline: UAE eases Ebola-related visa and entry restrictions for Ugandans
article.articleSummary: UAE eases Ebola-related entry restrictions for Ugandan nationals, announced November 11, 2026. The National Emergency Crisis and Disaster Management Authority (NCEMA), MoHAP, and ICP lift the visa-suspension introduced in June 2026, permitting Ugandan nationals to enter the UAE provided at least 21 days have elapsed since departure from Uganda. The revised rules extend entry to Ugandan students enrolled in UAE institutions before June 2026 (and their families), administrative staff at the Ugandan Embassy in the UAE with ordinary passports (and families), and holders of Ugandan diplomatic or special passports under approved health procedures. Medical and humanitarian cases are assessed individually, with travelers for medical treatment required to submit a medical report detailing diagnosis, treating facility, and treatment start date. Precautions for the Democratic Republic of the Congo and South Sudan remain in effect; authorities will monitor epidemiological developments and adjust measures as needed.

triage.headline_ja: UAE、ウガンダ人に対するエボラ関連のビザ・入国制限を緩和
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱に関連した国際的な渡航制限措置の緩和であり、IHR基準（深刻性・異常性・国際拡大リスク・渡航制限）の複数に該当するためフルRRAでの確認が妥当。
triage.notes: 記事の主眼はウガンダ人に対するUAEの入国制限緩和だが、ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。DRCについては『引き続き予防措置が有効』と明記されており、エボラ関連の懸念国として言及されているため verified_locations に含めた。南スーダン・UAEは対象国リスト外のため除外。

article.articleHeadline: RDC : L'impact dramatique de l'insécurité sur la riposte contre Ebola dans l'est congolais - Mali Actu
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: DRC: The dramatic impact of insecurity on the Ebola response in eastern Congo - Mali Actu
article.articleSummary: In eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, insecurity severely hampers the Ebola response, as attacks on health facilities in Beni and Mabalako (North Kivu) in early November disrupt the epidemiological surveillance chain. The World Health Organization, via Dr. Roselyne Belizaire, warns that more than 60% of contacts in the affected area have fallen out of tracing, and confirmed cases under treatment have dwindled. North Kivu and Ituri have long hosted armed conflict, complicating outbreak response and exacerbating endemic diseases such as cholera. Humanitarian access is restricted and mass displacement erodes on-the-ground prophylaxis and vaccination efforts. Experts emphasize that success requires more than biomedical measures: establishing safe humanitarian corridors and rebuilding trust with communities. Without effective pacification, containment of this highly contagious pathogen will remain structurally compromised.

triage.headline_ja: DRC：コンゴ東部におけるエボラ対応への治安悪化の深刻な影響 - Mali Actu
triage.triage_reason: WHO専門家がコンタクトトレーシングの60%以上が追跡不能になっていると警告しており、武力紛争により高致死率のエボラ対応が構造的に機能不全に陥っている深刻な事例。
triage.notes: 北キブ州・イツリ州における武力紛争がエボラ対応（接触者追跡、ワクチン接種、医療施設への攻撃）を著しく妨げており、コレラなど他の風土病の悪化も懸念される。WHO（Dr. Roselyne Belizaire）が人道回廊の確立とコミュニティとの信頼回復の必要性を強調している。

article.articleHeadline: 秋冬流感流行季逐渐开启 家庭备药别跟风__新快网
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Autumn–winter influenza season is gradually under way; households should not stock up on medicines just to follow the trend.
article.articleSummary: China’s autumn–winter influenza season has started, with multiple strains co-circulating and weak cross-protection between them. The season generally runs November–March; vaccination remains beneficial even if started late, with best timing in September–October. Influenza begins abruptly with high fever and severe systemic symptoms, unlike the common cold, and can lead to complications, especially in children, people aged ≥65, pregnant women, and those with chronic diseases or immune suppression. Severe signs include chest tightness, shortness of breath, confusion, or persistent fever; encephalitis risk may appear in children. Do not stockpile medicines; use antipyretics and cough/remedy products under medical guidance. Lianhua Qingwen is mentioned as a multi-virus remedy, to be used under professional instruction. Vaccines available in China are trivalent split, trivalent subunit, and trivalent live attenuated; split/subunit for ≥6 months, live attenuated for 3–17 years. Maintain hygiene, masking, ventilation, and distancing.

triage.headline_ja: 秋冬のインフルエンザ流行シーズンが徐々に始動、家庭での薬の買いだめは控えるよう呼びかけ
triage.triage_reason: 季節性インフルエンザに関する一般的な啓発記事であり、異常な流行や重症化の急増、国際的拡大リスクを示す情報はない。
triage.notes: 毎年の季節性インフルエンザに関する予防啓発・一般向け情報記事であり、特定の異常な集団発生やアウトブレイクの報告ではない。

article.articleHeadline: แพทย์ชี้คนเกิดก่อนปี 2523 เคยปลูกฝี มีภูมิคุ้มกันฝีดาษลิงข้ามสายพันธุ์
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Doctors say people born before 1980 who have received the smallpox vaccine have cross-species immunity to monkeypox.
article.articleSummary: As of 11 November 2026, in Thailand, people born before 1980 who received the smallpox vaccine may have cross-immunity to mpox (monkeypox), since both are orthopoxviruses. Immunity is estimated at about 80–85%. Thailand ended routine smallpox vaccination after 1980 following WHO eradication; the last natural smallpox case was in Somalia in 1977. Mpox spreads mainly through close contact with an infected person, especially touching vesicles, pustules, or skin lesions and exposure to mucous membranes of the mouth, eyes, or genitals. Transmission can begin at fever onset, even before rash, with highest risk during the vesicle/pustule phase; risk declines as lesions crust and heal. Casual contact in well-ventilated spaces has lower risk than prolonged close contact involving lesions or mucous membranes.

triage.headline_ja: 医師、1980年以前生まれで天然痘ワクチンを接種した人は、サル痘（Mpox）に対する交差免疫を持つと指摘
triage.triage_reason: 本記事は天然痘ワクチンとMpoxの交差免疫に関する一般的・解説的な医学情報であり、タイ国内での具体的な発生・症例報告ではないため、シグナルとして取り上げる根拠がない。
triage.notes: 記事は啓発的・解説的内容であり、タイやソマリアでの実際のMpox/天然痘の発生事例を報告するものではない。ソマリアの言及は1977年の天然痘根絶の歴史的事実に関するもので、現在の発生ではない。

article.articleHeadline: عدد حالات الإصابة بفيروس إيبولا في الكونغو يتجاوز 11 ألف حالة وسط استمرار تفشي المرض
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The number of Ebola virus infections in the Democratic Republic of the Congo exceeds 11,000 cases as the outbreak continues.
article.articleSummary: Democratic Republic of the Congo – As of 11 November 2026, Ebola virus disease infections in the country exceed 11,000, up from 10,000 confirmed cases reported last month by the Congolese government. The outbreak is described as the fastest-spreading Ebola crisis in history and has claimed nearly half of those infected, according to the Ministry of Health data, making it the deadliest Ebola outbreak on record in the DRC. Officials say the outbreak is ongoing and spreading across several African countries as authorities strive to curb transmission. The report underscores a high transmission pace and significant mortality, with the health ministry monitoring case counts and mortality to guide response and containment measures.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国でエボラウイルス感染者数が1万1千人を超え、流行が継続
triage.triage_reason: 致死率約50%の過去最大規模・最速拡大のエボラ流行であり、複数のアフリカ諸国への拡大も報じられているためIHR基準・WPRO基準の双方で複数該当し、フルRRAへ進むべき事案である。
triage.notes: 記事は『史上最速・最も致死的なエボラ流行』と報じており、周辺複数国への拡大にも言及しているが具体的な拡大国名は不明。続報でWHOの対応状況・渡航制限の有無を確認する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: कांगो में इबोला के मामले 11 हजार के पार तथा 5,387 लोगों की मौत
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola cases in Congo exceed 11,000, with 5,387 deaths.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo continues to escalate, with 11,042 infections and 5,387 deaths reported as of 11 November 2026. The Bundibugyo Ebola virus is responsible, spreading across eight of DR Congo’s 26 provinces, with outbreaks centered in Bunia. Since it was declared in mid-May, authorities have struggled to contain transmission amid armed conflict and fragile health systems. The case fatality rate is about 50%. There is currently no vaccine or specific treatment for Bundibugyo Ebola virus. triage.headline_ja: コンゴでエボラ感染者数が1万1000人を超え、5,387人が死亡

article.articleHeadline: DR Congo Ebola Cases Pass 11,000 as Death Toll Rises
article.articleSummary: DR Congo reports 11,042 confirmed Ebola cases and at least 5,387 deaths as of 2026-11-11, in its largest and deadliest outbreak. The epidemic is driven by the rare Bundibugyo strain, which kills about half of those infected, and is spreading across East, Central and West Africa—the widest geographic reach yet for Ebola on the continent. Eight of DR Congo’s 26 provinces are affected, with many deaths occurring outside treatment centres due to delayed detection, conflict and strained health services. The outbreak ranks as the second-largest and second-deadliest on record, behind the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic. The World Health Organization has approved clinical trials of two new Ebola vaccines, with results expected in early 2027; no vaccine or treatment exists specifically for Bundibugyo.

article.articleHeadline: High genomic diversity of dengue virus strains in Latin America and Asia-Pacific: insights from a phase 2 mosnodenvir clinical trial
article.articleSummary: dengue virus (DENV) genomic diversity assessed from a Phase 2 mosnodenvir prophylaxis trial conducted in 2023–2024 across Asia-Pacific and Latin America. Across 411 dengue index cases, DENV serotypes were assigned by RT-PCR; whole-genome sequencing was performed for a subset (n=150) from 30 sites in 7 countries. All four DENV serotypes cocirculated in both regions. DENV-1 was the predominant serotype (51.1%), with genotype V prevalent in Latin America, and genotypes I and IV in the Asia-Pacific region. Notably, DENV-3 and DENV-4 circulation rose in Latin America during 2023–2024. Time-resolved phylogenetics show the study captured a broad cross-section of contemporary DENV diversity during 2023–2024. These findings underscore the need for ongoing genomic surveillance for public health preparedness, highlighting a mosaic of local lineages and frequent virus re-introductions that could spark new outbreaks.

article.articleHeadline: Congo's Ebola outbreak tops 11,000 cases as disease keeps spreading
article.articleSummary: Congo's Ebola outbreak has surpassed 11,000 cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, with Health Ministry data on November 11, 2026 showing 11,042 infections and 5,387 deaths, the deadliest outbreak on record for the country and nearly half of those infected killed. The Bundibugyo virus responsible for the outbreak has no approved vaccine or treatment and has spread to eight of the 26 provinces. Declared in mid-May, the outbreak has unfolded amid ongoing conflict and a strained health system that hinder containment. Globally, outbreaks have occurred since 1976; the current event is the second-largest by cases and deaths, with infections and deaths already exceeding the time since declaration by multiple times compared with the West Africa outbreak of 2014–2016 (roughly 28,000 infections and >11,000 deaths). Medical evidence suggests infections were occurring months before declaration.

article.articleHeadline: Congo's Ebola outbreak tops 11,000 cases
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in Congo has surpassed 11,000 cases and 5,387 deaths as of 2026-11-11. Health ministry data show 11,042 infections across eight of the country’s 26 provinces, with Ituri and North Kivu as major hotspots. article.articleHeadline: Poor Glycemic Control Linked to Worse Tuberculosis Outcomes in
article.articleSummary: Poor glycemic control in patients with diabetes mellitus and pulmonary tuberculosis is linked to worse anti-TB outcomes. A systematic review and meta-analysis of 99 cohort studies (through March 1, 2026), mostly from China (96/99; two from India), found that poor glycemic control significantly lowers overall treatment efficacy (original OR 0.16, 95% CI 0.13–0.19; adjusted OR 0.22), sputum conversion (OR 0.19; adjusted 0.28), pulmonary lesion resolution (OR 0.17; adjusted 0.28), and cavity closure (OR 0.22; adjusted 0.23), while markedly increasing recurrence (OR 4.81). GRADE certainty is low for efficacy, sputum clearance, lesion resolution, and recurrence, and very low for cavity closure. Subgroup analyses showed no difference between fasting glucose and HbA1c in short-term outcomes; no clear dose–response with glycemic level or treatment duration. Limited secondary data suggest poorer post-treatment CD4+ changes and reduced reductions in hs-CRP/ESR with poor glycemic control.

article.articleHeadline: UAE lifts Ebola-related visa ban on Ugandan nationals
article.articleSummary: On 11 November 2026, the UAE lifts its visa suspension on Ugandan nationals imposed in June 2026 amid Ebola concerns in Central Africa. Ugandan applicants may again seek UAE visas, provided at least 21 days have passed since leaving Uganda. Exemptions cover Ugandan students in the UAE before June 2026 and their family members; Ugandan Embassy administrative staff with ordinary passports and their families; and holders of Ugandan diplomatic and special passports, subject to approved health procedures. Medical and humanitarian travel requests will be assessed individually; travellers seeking treatment must submit medical reports detailing diagnosis, treating facility, and planned start date. Restrictions remain for the Democratic Republic of the Congo and South Sudan, with precautionary entry measures continuing. The measures reflect sustained public health vigilance. Congo’s 17th Ebola epidemic has >7,000 cases and nearly 3,400 deaths; Uganda reported Ebola-free by late July; Saudi Arabia had separate June measures.

The update underscores a severe regional public health emergency with sustained fatalities as authorities continue response amid instability.

article.articleHeadline: Covid-19 volta a crescer em 18 estados; veja onde há aumento de casos
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: COVID-19 is rising again in 18 states; see where there is an increase in cases.
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 is rising again in Brazil, with 18 states and the Federal District reporting a recent uptick in mild infections, according to the Ministry of Health. Fiocruz’s InfoGripe notes signals of increased Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SRAG) associated with COVID-19 in Mato Grosso, Distrito Federal, Rio de Janeiro, São Paulo, and Santa Catarina, though hospitalizations and deaths remain well below 2025 levels and national risk is low. Common symptoms include fever, cough, sore throat, runny nose, fatigue and body aches; severe cases may cause breathing difficulties. Through Oct 31, 2026, Brazil recorded 118,851 influenza-like illness cases linked to COVID-19, about 68.8% lower than 2025; 3,400 SRAG cases and 437 deaths (as of Nov 4) are down about 63% and 69%. Sequencing of 2,199 samples (weeks 1–43, 2026) identified 127 lineages. Vaccination remains the main prevention; over 20.3 million doses distributed, 7.4 million administered; rapid tests and antivirals stocked in October.

triage.notes: ブラジル保健省・Fiocruz InfoGripeによる季節性の軽度症例増加の報告。入院・死亡は2025年比で大幅減少しており、国家リスクは低いとされる。継続的なサーベイランスのため経過観察とする。

article.articleHeadline: Bayi Bapil Usai Dipeluk Cium Keluarga, Virus Ini Bisa Jadi Pemicu
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Bapil Baby After Being Hugged and Kissed by Family, This Virus Could Be the Trigger
article.articleSummary: Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) poses a significant risk to newborns and infants under six months, with close family contact—hugs and kisses—raising transmission chances. In South Jakarta, Indonesia, RSV is a respiratory virus that typically presents with cold-like symptoms (runny nose, cough, sneezing, fever). While adults may have mild illness, infants can develop rapid breathing, chest retractions, lethargy or poor feeding, and blue-tinged lips; severe cases often require hospitalization. Hospitalizations for RSV peak early: about 50% occur in the first 3 months of life, and over 75% by 6 months. The tiny infant airways mean high viral loads can cause rapid breathing problems. Pregnant women are advised to consider RSV vaccination to protect newborns, as infancy RSV infection can increase the risk of asthma later in childhood. Most cases recover, but many infants need inpatient care as of 11 November 2026.

article.articleHeadline: Ébola: Surto na República Democrática do Congo ultrapassa 11 mil casos
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola: Outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo Surpasses 11,000 Cases.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has surpassed 11,000 cases, with 11,042 infections and 5,387 deaths; 2,990 recoveries and 651 hospitalised or isolated as of 9 November. Eastern provinces Ituri (57.7%) and North Kivu (32.7%) remain most affected. Declared in mid-May in Ituri, the Bundibugyo strain has no proven vaccine or treatment; two vaccines are in human trials, and Ervebo (Zaire strain) has been deployed in a large-scale campaign since late August, with animal studies showing cross-protection against Bundibugyo. WHO reports 79.7% contact-tracing. Ongoing violence and health-system gaps hamper containment; health workers have been attacked. The outbreak has spread to Uganda (outbreak ended 26 Aug: 20 cases, 15 imported), Kenya (9 cases), Nigeria (1 case), and a related case in France; four evacuees linked to DRC were sent to the Netherlands, Germany and United Kingdom. This is DRC’s 17th Ebola outbreak and the second-deadliest globally.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱：コンゴ民主共和国での発生が1万1千例を超える
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ（ブンディブギョ株）流行が1万1千例・死者5,387人に達し、ウガンダ・ケニア・ナイジェリア・フランスへの国際拡大も確認されており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルリスク評価に進むべき。
triage.notes: 記事はDRC（特にIturiと北キブ州）での流行を主題としており、ウガンダ・ケニア・ナイジェリア・フランス・オランダ・ドイツ・英国への拡大は対象国リスト外または輸入症例・退避者であるためverified_locationsには含めない。致死率が高く（約49%）、ワクチン未承認の新規株であることから重大性・異常性が高い。

article.articleHeadline: Kasus Campak Anak di Pangkalpinang Naik 70 Kasus, Dessy Minta Orang Tua Izinkan Imunisasi BIAS
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Measles Cases in Children in Pangkalpinang Increase by 70 Cases, Dessy Urges Parents to Allow BIAS Immunization.
article.articleSummary: Measles cases among children in Pangkalpinang, Indonesia, have risen to about 70 in 2026, more than doubling from roughly 30 last year. City officials urge parental consent for immunization, emphasizing the School Immunization Month (BIAS) program for 2026. Deputy Mayor Dessy Ayutrisna, during monitoring at SD Negeri 35 Pangkalpinang on November 11, 2026, stressed immunization as essential for child health and a basic right, urging broader participation beyond the schools visited. BIAS runs twice yearly, in August and November, targeting school-age children with vaccines aligned to age schedules. Health authorities continue socialization efforts, noting success depends on parental support. In November, vaccines administered through BIAS include DT, TD, and HPV, while the MR (measles-rubella) vaccination was completed in August. The outbreak focus remains measles prevention through expanded immunization coverage.

triage.headline_ja: パンカルピナンの小児麻疹症例が70件に増加、デッシー氏が保護者にBIAS予防接種の許可を呼びかけ
triage.triage_reason: 麻疹症例の増加は見られるが、重症度や国際的拡大の情報がなく、既存の予防接種プログラムで対応中であるため、フルRRAには至らないが経過観察が必要。
triage.notes: 地元自治体主導の予防接種推進活動が中心で、症例数の倍増は見られるが重症度・死亡等の情報はなし。局所的なアウトブレイク管理の範疇と考えられる。

article.articleHeadline: DR Congo Faces Growing Fears of a Cholera Resurgence
article.articleSummary: Cholera in the Democratic Republic of Congo has recorded more than 60,000 cases and 1,800 deaths since the beginning of the year, with the WHO Director-General calling it the worst outbreak in decades. The eastern North and South Kivu provinces have been hardest hit as violence and insecurity hinder containment. There are growing concerns about the disease spreading to Kinshasa amid the rainy season. Officials cite poor access to clean water and sanitation, underscoring the need for enhanced prevention, improved water infrastructure, and vaccination campaigns. Doctors Without Borders has expanded its response by providing medical care, safe drinking water and sanitation support, though ongoing insecurity, weak infrastructure, and limited healthcare access continue to hamper containment efforts.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国、コレラ再流行への懸念高まる
triage.triage_reason: DRCで60,000例以上・死者1,800人超の大規模コレラ流行が発生し、WHO事務局長が『数十年で最悪』と表明するなど深刻かつ異常な公衆衛生事象であり、フルリスク評価が必要と判断される。
triage.notes: 記事はDRC国内（特に北・南キブ州およびキンシャサへの拡大懸念）に焦点を当てており、国際的な越境拡大については言及がないため『不明』とした。WHOおよびMSFが既に対応に関与しており、国際支援の必要性は高い。

article.articleHeadline: إيبولا يضرب الكونغو الديمقراطية.. 11 ألف إصابة وأكثر من 5 آلاف وفاة
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola strikes the Democratic Republic of the Congo... 11,000 cases and more than 5,000 deaths.
article.articleSummary: Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has reached 11,042 confirmed cases and 5,387 deaths as of 11 November 2026, per government data cited by Reuters. The current outbreak, caused by the rare Bundibugyo Ebola virus strain, was declared in mid-May and ranks as the second-largest and deadliest on record after West Africa’s 2014–2016 epidemic. Eight of the country’s 26 provinces have reported cases. A large number of deaths occur outside treatment centers due to delayed detection, ongoing conflict, and overwhelmed health services, accelerating spread versus prior outbreaks. The outbreak has been reported across eastern, central, and western Africa, making it the most geographically widespread Ebola event in the continent to date. There are no approved vaccines or therapeutics for the Bundibugyo strain, complicating response efforts.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱がコンゴ民主共和国で拡大…感染者1万1000人、死者5000人超
triage.triage_reason: 致死率の高いエボラ出血熱が11,000人超感染・5,000人超死亡という大規模流行であり、ワクチン・治療薬未承認かつ複数州・複数地域に拡大しているため、IHR基準・WPRO基準の多くに該当する。
triage.notes: 記事はコンゴ民主共和国（DRC）が主題。Angolaは発生地域に含まれるが対象国リストに無く、サマリー内でも言及されていないため除外。Bundibugyo株による過去最大級かつ地理的に最も広範囲なエボラ流行とされ、ワクチン・治療薬未承認である点が特に懸念材料。

article.articleHeadline: Congo's Ebola outbreak passes 11,000 cases with 5,387 dead
article.articleSummary: Democratic Republic of the Congo's Ebola outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo strain, has surpassed 11,000 confirmed cases and 5,387 deaths as of November 10, marking the largest and deadliest outbreak in DR Congo and the second-largest and second-deadliest on record globally, behind 2014-2016 West Africa. The outbreak began May 15 and was declared a public health emergency of international concern two days later. There is no licensed vaccine or approved specific treatment for Bundibugyo; the Ervebo vaccine targets the Zaire strain. Cases are confirmed across eight of DR Congo's 26 provinces and 67 health zones, with Ituri province most affected (28 of 36 health zones). Transmission is slowing in some areas, but insecurity and displacement create new hotspots. WHO approved two new vaccine clinical trials with results expected early 2027; MSF has urged lifting Ervebo's restrictions to research-use in this outbreak.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ出血熱流行、感染者数11,000人、死者5,387人を超える
triage.triage_reason: WHOによりPHEIC（国際的に懸念される公衆衛生上の緊急事態）が宣言された史上第2位の規模・致死数のエボラ流行であり、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: Bundibugyo株による流行で既承認ワクチン（Ervebo）はZaire株対象のため有効性が限定的。治安不安・住民移動により新規ホットスポット発生の懸念あり。WHOが新規ワクチン臨床試験を承認（結果は2027年初頭予定）。

article.articleHeadline: Covid em alta no Brasil: quem pode tomar a vacina, quando fazer o teste e os sintomas; um guia completo sobre a infecção
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: COVID-19 on the Rise in Brazil: Who Can Get the Vaccine, When to Get Tested, and the Symptoms; A Comprehensive Guide to the Infection.
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 activity is rising in Brazil, with 118,851 coronavirus-related respiratory syndrome cases reported this year through the 4th, and a six-week upward trend. Increases span Alagoas, Bahia, Ceará, Distrito Federal, Espírito Santo, Goiás, Minas Gerais, Mato Grosso, Paraíba, Pernambuco, Piauí, Paraná, Rio de Janeiro, Rondônia, Roraima, Rio Grande do Sul, Santa Catarina, and São Paulo. SRAG hospitalizations are up in Mato Grosso, Distrito Federal, São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, and Santa Catarina. Lab positivity (ITpS) rose from 6.62% end-September to 16.66% last week, the highest since March 2025. Vaccination guidance: children 6 months–5 years get three doses; 5–59 years without prior vaccination get a single dose. No routine boosters for the general population; boosters advised for pregnant people, seniors >60 and immunocompromised (every six months), and annual boosters for several high-risk groups. Transmission mainly via close contact, droplets and aerosols.

triage.headline_ja: ブラジルでCOVID-19が増加：誰がワクチンを接種できるか、いつ検査すべきか、症状について；感染症に関する完全ガイド
triage.triage_reason: ブラジル国内でCOVID-19症例・入院が増加傾向にあるが、既知の季節性変動の範囲内であり、国際的拡大や渡航制限の兆候はないため、経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 記事は一般向けのCOVID-19ガイド記事であり、ブラジル国内の複数州で症例・入院が増加している季節性の動向を報告している。新規変異株や異常な重症度についての言及はなく、既知の疾患の国内動向報告にとどまる。

article.articleHeadline: Случаите на ебола в Конго вече са над 11 000
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola cases in Congo are already over 11,000.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has surpassed 11,000 confirmed cases, with 11,042 cases and 5,387 deaths reported. The neighboring Republic of the Congo has no reported cases. The outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo ebolavirus variant, was declared in mid-May; there are no approved treatments or vaccines for this variant. It is the second-largest Ebola outbreak by cases and deaths, after West Africa's 2014–2016 epidemic (over 28,600 cases and more than 11,000 deaths). Eight of 26 DRC provinces have been affected, with many fatalities occurring outside health facilities. Slow detection, ongoing armed conflict, and an overwhelmed health system have accelerated spread. The outbreak now spans East, Central, and West Africa, marking the widest geographic reach of Ebola on the continent to date.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ症例数が既に11,000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: DRCで11,000例超・5,387人死亡の大規模エボラ流行であり、承認された治療薬・ワクチンがないBundibugyoエボラウイルス変異株による流行で、複数州・複数地域に拡大しているためIHR基準・WPRO基準ともに該当数が多い。

article.articleHeadline: Nigeria encadena 21 días sin nuevos casos de ébola tras detectar un contagio importado
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Nigeria records 21 days without new Ebola cases after detecting an imported case.
article.articleSummary: Nigeria reported 21 days without new Ebola cases after an imported Bundibugyo virus infection detected on Oct 20, 2026. By Nov 9, 2026, only that single imported case had been confirmed; 62 contacts were identified, with 34 completing the 21‑day follow‑up and 28 still under surveillance. Health officials stressed that monitoring can identify symptoms early and that a contact may not be infected. The index patient is a Swiss citizen of Ugandan origin who returned to Abuja after holidays in Uganda and did not transit through the DRC. Genomic analysis links the Nigerian virus to a strain seen in Kenya, though this does not prove direct transmission; AU agencies have suggested possible cross‑over at Entebbe airport on Oct 3. The ongoing Congo outbreak since May 15 involves eight provinces with 11,042 cases and 5,387 deaths. Uganda reports 20 cases (15 imported from DRC), Kenya 9 cases (2 deaths), and France 1 case; there have been evacuations to the Netherlands (1), the United Kingdom (1), and Germany (2). Bundibugyo lacks a specific treatment; vaccines in human trials are proceeding.

triage.headline_ja: ナイジェリア、輸入エボラ症例検出後21日間新規感染なしを記録
triage.triage_reason: DRCを起点とする大規模エボラ流行（患者11,042人、死亡5,387人）が複数国に国際的拡大しており、IHR基準複数該当かつWPRO基準も複数該当するためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 記事はナイジェリアの輸入症例収束を報じているが、背景にあるDRCでの大規模流行（5月15日以降、8州で11,042症例・5,387死亡）が本イベントの核心であり、ウガンダ・ケニア・ナイジェリア・フランスへの国際拡大と欧州への患者搬送（オランダ・英国・ドイツ）も発生している。対象国リストではDRCのみが該当。

article.articleHeadline: New Covid-19 Variant Alert! First PJ.2.1 Infection Report Surfaces, WHO Warns; Should Indians Worry?
article.articleSummary: PJ.2.1 is a new COVID-19 variant monitored by the WHO as of 11 November 2026. Symptoms resemble cold and flu, making testing essential, with no current evidence of increased severity. First detected June 2026 (Canada identified in May 2026 per a research letter). Wastewater analyses show PJ.2.1 as the fastest-growing variant in the United States; it has been detected in Australia, Singapore, Spain, and in about 19 countries. It carries a highly mutated spike protein (a “saltation” variant) but is not believed to markedly evade immunity; fatigue may be prolonged in some cases. No confirmed Indian cases, and no new advisory from India's Union Health Ministry. Hospitals are not under pandemic pressure; India maintains surveillance via IDSP and ICMR, building on experience from earlier Omicron-descended waves such as JN.1, which did not trigger a surge in severe disease. Elderly individuals should remain cautious.

triage.headline_ja: 新型コロナウイルス変異株アラート！初のPJ.2.1感染例が報告、WHOが警告 ― インド人は心配すべきか？
triage.triage_reason: WHOが監視対象とする高度変異（サルテーション型）の新変異株PJ.2.1が既に約19か国で検出されており、国際的拡大が確認されているため、IHR基準（異常性・国際拡大）が2つ該当しフルリスク評価が妥当と判断した。
triage.notes: インドでは現時点で確定症例はなく、保健省からの新たな注意喚起も出ていないため、インドを実際の発生国として含めることは適切でないと判断した。対象国リストの中で実発生が確認されている国はないため、verified_locationsは空配列とした。

article.articleHeadline: சென்னை மாநகராட்சியில் டெங்கு உள்ளிட்ட காய்ச்சல் தடுப்பு நடவடிக்கைகள் தீவிரம்
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Dengue and other fever prevention measures have been intensified in the Greater Chennai Corporation.
article.articleSummary: Dengue and fever prevention measures have been intensified in Greater Chennai Corporation, Tamil Nadu, ahead of the northeast monsoon. About 3,703 workers are engaged in dengue control and vector suppression. From Oct 15 to Nov 9, 2026, 2,359 fever camps reached 78,996 people; by Nov 10, 2026, 2,430 camps served 81,199. Daily camps target early detection and treatment in high-risk areas, including slums and flood-prone zones. Vector-control includes door-to-door surveys, removing breeding sites, larviciding water tanks and drains, fogging, and intensified cleanliness drives; 372 hotspots are monitored. Water testing shows adequate residual chlorine: 515 samples on Nov 9; 1,166 samples on Nov 10. Bleaching powder stock is 53,405 kg, with 150 tonnes more planned. Healthcare infrastructure comprises 140 urban PHCs, 200 urban welfare centers, 16 CHCs, 3 maternity hospitals, a 360-facility infectious disease hospital network, and 10 dialysis centers. 237 near-term pregnant mothers were contacted by phone.

triage.headline_ja: チェンナイ市当局、デング熱を含む発熱予防対策を強化
triage.triage_reason: モンスーン前の例年実施されるデング熱・発熱予防の行政対策に関する報道であり、具体的な症例数・死亡者数の急増や異常なアウトブレイクを示す情報はない。
triage.notes: 記事はチェンナイ市当局による季節性のデング熱予防・媒介生物対策（防疫員配置、発熱キャンプ、塩素消毒、漂白粉備蓄等）の実施状況を報告する行政広報的内容であり、具体的な感染者数・死亡者数の記載はなく、異常な流行を示す根拠はない。

article.articleHeadline: Nipah Virus Transmission in Bangladesh and India Is Overdispersed and
article.articleSummary: Nipah virus transmission in Bangladesh and India (2001–2026) is self-limiting on average but highly overdispersed. Analyzing 323 cases across 67 outbreaks from 27 sources, researchers used a hierarchical Bayesian negative binomial model on 137 transmission pairs to estimate key epidemiological metrics. The pooled median reproduction number (R) is 0.43 (95% CrI 0.26–0.75) and the pooled offspring dispersion parameter (k) is 0.04 (0.03–0.06); the serial interval is 13.3 days (12.8–13.8). Country-level estimates show India with R 0.47 (0.22–0.98) and k 0.03 (0.02–0.06), Bangladesh with R 0.35 (0.19–0.63) and k 0.05 (0.03–0.09). The results indicate pronounced overdispersion, meaning a small fraction of cases drive most secondary transmission rather than uniform spread. Transmission is driven by the Nipah Bangladesh genotype and Nipah India genotype, underscoring the benefit of targeted public health containment, including contact tracing and quarantine.

triage.headline_ja: バングラデシュとインドにおけるニパウイルス感染は過分散的かつ自己制限的である
triage.triage_reason: 本記事は2001〜2026年の過去症例データを用いた学術的な数理疫学モデリング研究であり、新規発生や現在進行中のアウトブレイクを報告するものではない。
triage.notes: 本記事はニパウイルスの伝播動態（R値・分散パラメータk）に関する過去データの統計解析研究であり、新規アウトブレイクの発生報告ではない。研究結果は、伝播が自己制限的だが過分散（少数の症例が二次感染の大半を引き起こす）であることを示しており、的を絞った接触者追跡・隔離の有効性を支持する内容。バングラデシュは対象国リストに含まれないため除外し、インドのみ記載した。

article.articleHeadline: इबोला का खतरा! उत्तराखंड में अलर्ट, 21 दिन तक यात्रियों की होगी निगरानी
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola Threat! Uttarakhand on Alert, Passengers to Be Monitored for 21 Days.
article.articleSummary: Uttarakhand is on high alert over Ebola amid rising infections in Africa. Travelers returning from affected countries will be monitored for 21 days, with district surveillance units updating health records via a state portal. Hospitals must maintain isolation wards, dedicated ambulances, trained health workers, PPE kits, and N-95 masks; AIIMS Rishikesh is designated as the isolation hospital for suspected or confirmed Ebola cases. Contacts of suspected patients will also be monitored for 21 days, and Rapid Response Teams activated. Residents are urged to monitor health and report travel history if fever or symptoms appear. Kashipur area has 15 families with members in South Africa, but none have returned in the past month and no Ebola case is reported there. Symptoms include fever, weakness, headaches, sore throat, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain, bleeding gums or nose, red eyes, rashes, and blood in vomit or stool. Dr. KK Aggarwal, Health Director, Kumaon, emphasizes vigilance.

triage.headline_ja: エボラの脅威！ウッタラーカンド州で警戒、渡航者を21日間監視
triage.triage_reason: インド・ウッタラーカンド州でのエボラ警戒態勢と渡航者監視に関する記事であり、インド国内での実際の感染事例は報告されていない。アフリカでの感染増加が背景にあるが具体的な発生国は不明のため、続報を注視する必要がある。
triage.notes: 記事はインドにおける予防的な監視・警戒体制の強化を報じたものであり、インド国内でのエボラ確定症例は報告されていない。感染拡大の震源地とされる「アフリカ」の具体的な国名（対象国リスト該当国）は記事中に明示されていないため、verified_locationsは空配列とした。カシプール地域で南アフリカに親族を持つ家庭が言及されているが、South Africa(953987)は対象国リストに含まれない。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola outbreak has now infected more than 11,000 people and half have died
article.articleSummary: DRC Ebola outbreak (Bundibugyo virus) has surpassed 11,000 cases, with 11,042 infections and 5,387 deaths, in what is described as the country’s deadliest outbreak. Declared mid-May, it has spread to eight of the DRC’s 26 provinces, with Ituri and North Kivu as major hotspots. Containment hampered by armed conflict, health-system strain, poor roads, and community mistrust; health facilities and workers targeted. The Bundibugyo virus has no approved vaccine or treatment. The outbreak has reached neighboring countries, with cases in Uganda, Kenya and Nigeria. Separately, a British healthcare worker infected in DRC was evacuated to the UK and is in isolation at the Royal Free Hospital; UKHSA says the public risk remains very low. Ebola transmission requires direct contact with infected bodily fluids; incubation 2–21 days; early symptoms include fever, aches, fatigue, progressing to diarrhoea, vomiting and bleeding.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱の流行、感染者数が11,000人を超え、その半数が死亡

triage.notes: 記事はDRCでのエボラ流行を主題とし、Uganda・Kenya・Nigeria・UKへの波及も報告されているが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsから除外。ワクチン・治療法が存在しないBundibugyo種であることも重大性を高めている。

article.articleHeadline: Случаите на ебола в ДР Конго надхвърлиха 11 000, а починалите са 5387
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo surpassed 11,000, and the deaths were 5,387.
article.articleSummary: 11,042 Ebola cases and at least 5,387 deaths have been reported in eight of the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s 26 provinces, marking the largest and deadliest Ebola outbreak in the country’s history. The outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus and is hampered by armed conflict, delayed detection, and an overwhelmed health system, accelerating spread. It has extended across East, Central, and West Africa, representing the widest geographic reach of any Ebola outbreak on the continent. There is no vaccine or specific treatment for Bundibugyo; two vaccine trials are expected to yield results in early 2027. Incubation is 2–21 days; initial symptoms include high fever, fatigue, headache, muscle and throat pain, followed by vomiting, diarrhea, rash, liver and kidney dysfunction, and in severe cases internal/external bleeding and multi-organ failure. Transmission occurs via contact with blood or bodily fluids from humans or animals; monoclonal antibody therapies exist for Ebola (Zaire ebolavirus), though applicability to Bundibugyo is not specified.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国でのエボラ出血熱患者数が11,000人を超え、死者数は5,387人に達した

triage.notes: モザンビーク・アンゴラはBluedotの発生地域に含まれるが、記事サマリーでは主題としてDRCのみが具体的に言及されており、他国での感染拡大の詳細は確認できないため除外。Bundibugyoエボラウイルス株にはワクチン・特異的治療法が存在せず、2027年初頭にワクチン試験結果が期待されている。

article.articleHeadline: Congo Ebola Outbreak Crosses 11,000 Cases, Can India Help?
article.articleSummary: DRC Ebola outbreak caused by Bundibugyo strain has reached 11,042 confirmed cases and 5,387 deaths across eight of 26 provinces, as of November 11, 2026. Declared May 15, the outbreak is the country’s deadliest, with no approved vaccine or specific treatment; supportive care remains primary. Case fatality about 49%. Transmission is hindered by insecurity, weak health systems, and limited access; attacks on health workers and poor transport complicate case finding and contact tracing. By November 3, 10,668 cases and 5,198 deaths were reported; many deaths (335 of 512 since Oct 21) occurred in communities outside treatment centers. Beyond DRC, cases reported in Kenya and Nigeria. WHO supports Tumaini vaccine trial in Bunia, Ituri; initially evaluating Ervebo, now adding experimental candidates: ChAdOx1 (Oxford/SII) and Moderna's mRNA-1469. ChAdOx1 inclusion recommended; Serum Institute of India collaborating with Oxford; no publicly confirmed Indian government aid.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ出血熱、感染者数が11,000人を突破 ― インドは支援できるか？

triage.notes: 記事はインドが国際支援（ワクチン供与等）を検討すべきかを論じているが、インド国内での感染確認情報はないため verified_locations には含めない。ケニア・ナイジェリアへの感染拡大が報告されているが、両国は対象国リストに含まれないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: La República Democrática del Congo supera la barrera de los 11.000 casos de ébola, incluidos 5.387 muertos
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Democratic Republic of the Congo surpasses the 11,000-case Ebola threshold, including 5,387 deaths.
article.articleSummary: DRC's Ebola outbreak has surpassed 11,000 confirmed infections, with 5,387 deaths (case fatality rate 48.8%), per INSP data through November 9, 2026. Total: 11,042 infections, 2,990 recoveries, and 651 hospitalized or in isolation; contact tracing at 79.7%. Ituri (epicenter) and North Kivu account for 57.7% and 32.7% of new cases, respectively, with 67 health zones across eight provinces affected (Ituri, North Kivu, Tshopo, Bas-Uélé, Haut-Uélé, South Kivu, Ubangui-Sud, Ubangui-Nord). The Bundibugyo Ebola strain has no specific treatments; vaccines in Phase 1 trials have been safe, and Ervebo, begun in August, shows positive signals against Bundibugyo in animals. The outbreak has spread to Uganda (20 cases, 2 deaths; Uganda declared end of outbreak Aug 26), Kenya (9 cases, 2 deaths), Nigeria (1), and a France-linked case; four evacuees to the Netherlands (1), Germany (2), and the United Kingdom (1). Transmission is via contact with bodily fluids; symptoms include fever, hemorrhagic signs, vomiting, and diarrhea.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国、エボラ出血熱患者数が1万1000人を超え、死者5387人に

triage.notes: ウガンダ、ケニア、ナイジェリア、フランス・オランダ・ドイツ・英国への波及が報告されているが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsから除外。主たる発生国はDRCのみ。

article.articleHeadline: ฤดูหนาวนี้ต้องระวัง! เตือนรับมือโรคติดต่อ-ภัยสุขภาพ ลดเสี่ยงเจ็บป่วย-เสียชีวิต
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: This winter, stay vigilant! A warning to cope with infectious diseases and health hazards, reducing the risk of illness and death.
article.articleSummary: Winter in Thailand heightens spread of respiratory infections: influenza, pneumonia, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and COVID-19, with fever, cough, sore throat, runny nose, headache, and body aches; some cases progress to dyspnea or pneumonia, especially in children, the elderly, and those with underlying conditions. Prevention emphasizes masking in crowded or high-risk settings, frequent handwashing, social distancing, vaccination per doctor’s advice, and rest/limited contact when ill. Food- and waterborne disease includes acute diarrhea from contaminated food/water, presenting with watery stools, abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting; guidance centers on “cook thoroughly, drink clean water, use clean utensils, wash hands before meals and after toilets,” and avoiding raw foods. Vector-borne risks include malaria and scrub typhus in forested areas; travelers should prevent bites and seek prompt medical care with travel history upon fever after return. Additional hazards include winter-related mortality, especially among vulnerable groups; advice covers warmth, vitamin-C–rich foods, avoiding alcohol, careful medication considerations, and proper ventilation for gas water heaters. Public health authorities in Thailand coordinate monitoring and risk communication via SRRT teams and 12 regional offices.

triage.headline_ja: この冬は要注意！感染症・健康被害への対策を呼びかけ、病気と死亡のリスクを減らす
triage.triage_reason: 季節性の一般的な感染症対策に関する啓発記事であり、特定の異常な集団発生や急増を示す情報はないため、シグナルとしての基準を満たさない。
triage.notes: タイ保健当局による冬季の季節性感染症（インフルエンザ、RSV、COVID-19等）と食品媒介・ベクター媒介疾患への一般的注意喚起記事。具体的な症例数増加や異常事態の報告はなし。

article.articleHeadline: Sơ cứu bé trai co giật do cúm A
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: First aid for a boy having a seizure due to influenza A
article.articleSummary: Hanoi, Vietnam: a two-year-old boy presented with fever 39.2°C and a febrile seizure attributed to influenza A. At VNVC Khai Sơn on 1 November, medical staff provided urgent first aid—loosening clothing, giving oxygen, and cooling—achieving a temperature drop to 37.5°C, heart rate 125/min, and normal oxygen saturation within about 25 minutes. An ambulance transported him to a local hospital, where influenza A was diagnosed; he remained febrile into the evening and was later transferred to Vietnam National Pediatric Hospital for continued monitoring. After several days of treatment, he recovered and was discharged. The report notes febrile seizures are common in children aged 6 months to 5 years; caregivers should avoid restraining the child, protect the head, and call emergency services (115) for first-time or prolonged seizures or respiratory distress. Vaccination and hygiene remain key, with Vietnam offering injectable and nasal influenza vaccines for different age groups.

triage.headline_ja: インフルエンザAによるけいれんを起こした男児への応急処置
triage.triage_reason: 個別の小児症例報告であり、季節性インフルエンザAによる熱性けいれんという一般的な臨床事象。公衆衛生上の異常性や国際的拡大リスクは認められない。

article.articleHeadline: Congo's Ebola outbreak tops 11,000 cases as disease keeps spreading
article.articleSummary: Congo's Ebola outbreak caused by Bundibugyo virus has reached 11,042 infections and 5,387 deaths as of 2026-11-11, marking Congo's deadliest outbreak. Declared in mid-May, the outbreak has spread to eight of the country’s 26 provinces, with Ituri and North Kivu as major hotspots. The Bundibugyo virus has no known vaccine or treatment, complicating containment amid armed conflict, a fragile health system, poor roads, and community mistrust and misinformation. Health facilities and professionals have been targeted, hindering response efforts. The outbreak has crossed borders, with cases reported in Uganda, Kenya, and Nigeria. Authorities urge an immediate halt to fighting to allow unrestricted access for responders and call for intensified surveillance and community engagement to slow transmission as the virus continues to spread.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ出血熱アウトブレイク、感染者数が11,000人を超え、感染拡大続く
triage.triage_reason: 致死率の高いエボラ（ブンディブギョウイルス）が11,000人超の感染、5,000人超の死亡を記録し、複数国への越境拡大が確認されているため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する重大事案。
triage.notes: 記事はウガンダ・ケニア・ナイジェリアへの越境を報じているが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsには含めず。DRCが主たる発生地域として該当。武力紛争・医療アクセス制限・ワクチン治療法不在という極めて深刻な状況であり、フルリスク評価が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Instituto Butantan cria nanopartículas de prata contra esquistossomose e Aedes aegypti
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Butantan Institute develops silver nanoparticles against schistosomiasis and Aedes aegypti.
article.articleSummary: Butantan Institute in São Paulo, Brazil, developed silver nanoparticles via green nanotechnology using Aspergillus tubingensis secretions to combat Schistosoma mansoni cercariae and Aedes aegypti larvae. In laboratory tests, the nanoparticles at low concentrations achieved 100% killing of cercariae after two hours, offering a strategy to interrupt schistosomiasis transmission by targeting the infective stage rather than snail hosts. Biomphalaria glabrata snail stages were variably affected, with embryos more sensitive than adults. For Aedes aegypti, 4th-stage larvae exposed for 48 hours showed near-total larvicidal lethality, addressing vector-control challenges amid insecticide resistance. Ecotoxicology assessments, conducted with bioindicators including zebrafish, Daphnia magna, Cypricercus centrura, tilapia, lambari, cará, and ghost shrimp, evaluated environmental safety and selectivity, reporting preserved aquatic ecosystems. The study, led by Ana Olivia de Souza, also notes INPI patent protection and publication in Environmental Science: Nano, highlighting Brazil’s innovative approach to infectious disease control.

triage.headline_ja: ブタンタン研究所、住血吸虫症とネッタイシマカ対策の銀ナノ粒子を開発

article.articleHeadline: Ebola outbreak in Africa: Can the virus spread to India? Docotor explains risks
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in Africa, centered in the Democratic Republic of Congo, with more than 11,000 infections and over 5,300 deaths, raises concerns about spread to India. Dr. Randeep Guleria explains transmission is not airborne; infection occurs via direct contact with infected bodily fluids and is only contagious after symptoms develop. Incubation is 2–21 days, during which transmission is unlikely. Close contact with secretions drives spread; healthcare workers must use strict protective measures. Ebola is a zoonosis mainly in Central/Western Africa and can involve non-human primates. A recovered patient from Sierra Leone traveled to India in 2014, with the virus persisting in semen up to three months and in tears. Early signs include fever, body aches, sore throat, abdominal pain, diarrhoea; later stages involve bleeding, DIC, and ARDS. CFR can reach ~50%; recovery is possible with supportive care, though post-recovery issues may persist. Vigilance, screening and infection control; monitor travelers from affected regions.

triage.headline_ja: アフリカでのエボラ出血熱流行：インドへの拡大はあるか？医師がリスクを解説
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ流行は11,000人超の感染・致死率約50%と深刻で、ヒト-ヒト感染リスクと流行継続が確認され、インドでの社会的関心も高いためフルRRAへの移行が妥当。
triage.notes: 記事はインド向け一般メディアによる解説記事で、インドへの感染拡大可能性を医師が否定的に説明している。実際の発生国はDRCのみで、インドおよびシエラレオネ（2014年の過去事例）は発生国として含めない。

article.articleHeadline: 콩고 에볼라 감염 1만 1000명 돌파했다
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola infections in Congo surpass 11,000.
article.articleSummary: DRC Ebola outbreak surpasses 11,000 confirmed cases, with 5,387 deaths (case fatality ~48.8%), as of November 10 local time; the largest Ebola outbreak in Congo's history and the second-largest worldwide. The tally lists 11,042 confirmed infections and 5,387 deaths. Declared mid-May, the surge is hindered by armed conflict, weak health systems, and delays in case detection, with many deaths occurring in communities before reaching facilities. The outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, for which no approved vaccines or therapies proven effective exist. Spread has reached 8 of the DRC's 26 provinces, with related infections reported in eastern, central, and western Africa regions. The WHO is conducting clinical trials for vaccine candidates.

article.articleHeadline: Ülkedeki salgında can kaybı 5 bini aştı! 'Tedavi ya da aşısı yok'
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The death toll in the country's outbreak has surpassed 5,000! 'There is no treatment or vaccine'

There is no approved treatment or vaccine for this form. The event is described as the second-largest and most deadly Ebola outbreak recorded since the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic, underscoring the ongoing public health challenges posed by Ebola virus disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

article.articleHeadline: UAE lifts Ebola-related visa suspension for Ugandans | The National
article.articleSummary: UAE lifts visa suspension for Ugandans amid Ebola outbreak. Ugandan passport holders may enter the UAE once at least 21 days have passed since leaving Uganda. The measures, announced by UAE authorities, suspend new visas for the Democratic Republic of the Congo and South Sudan, while allowing Ugandans. Transit through the UAE remains subject to the 21-day rule outside the three African countries. Ugandan students enrolled in UAE institutions before June 2026, and their families, will be admitted under approved procedures. Administrative staff at the Ugandan embassy with ordinary passports and their families may enter; holders of Ugandan diplomatic or special passports are allowed under health procedures for exempted categories, in coordination with authorities. Humanitarian and medical cases will be assessed individually; medical travel requires approved reports detailing diagnosis, facility, and treatment date. Authorities will monitor the situation and update measures as needed.

triage.headline_ja: UAE、ウガンダ人に対するエボラ関連ビザ停止措置を解除

triage.notes: 記事はUAEによる渡航制限政策が主題だが、根本的な感染症イベントはDRC・ウガンダ・南スーダンでのエボラ流行。対象国リストにはDRCのみ含まれるため、verified_locationsはDRCのみとした。ウガンダ・南スーダン・UAEは対象国リスト外。

article.articleHeadline: 39岁明星经纪人染疫！短短一个月白肺离世
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: 39-year-old celebrity agent infected! In just one month, died of white lung.
article.articleSummary: Hao Boyan (also Hao Jing’an), a 39-year-old Beijing-based celebrity agent, died on November 9, 2026, after a COVID-19 infection that began in late September. He reportedly endured at home for over a month before his lungs turned white and perforated, with intubation on hospital admission; he died at 11:00 am in Beijing and was cremated the same day, with his ashes returned to Shandong. Tributes from entertainment colleagues followed his death. Separately, director Jiang Xiaoyu (Jiang Xi), 56, died in Beijing on November 1, potentially from a stroke; his mother had died about a month earlier. The article notes renewed COVID-19 resurgence in mainland China, with officials citing multiple circulating viruses, rising thromboembolism, and intensified disinfection measures, while alleging opacity around pandemic news.

triage.headline_ja: 39歳の芸能マネージャーが感染！わずか1ヶ月で「白肺」となり死亡

triage.notes: 記事は著名人個別事例の死亡報道が主体で、COVID-19再流行についての記述は具体的データに欠け、政治的批判色の強い媒体（阿波罗网）からの発信である点に留意が必要。公式統計や当局発表の裏付けが取れ次第、再評価を推奨。

article.articleHeadline: 北京经纪人郝泊言染新冠去世 年仅39岁
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Beijing-based talent agent Hao Boyan dies of COVID-19 at age 39.
article.articleSummary: Beijing-based talent agent Hao Boyan (aka Hao Jing’an), founder of Maier Culture and host of Bo Yan Meeting Hall, died in Beijing on November 9 at age 39 after contracting COVID-19 in late September and delaying medical care. He was hospitalized for over 20 days; his condition worsened with lung perforation and systemic dysbiosis (blood in stool) requiring tracheal intubation and ventilation. His company confirmed the illness; he had still been recording the show 12 days before death. Cremation occurred that afternoon, and his ashes returned to his native Shandong province. On November 11, authorities reported multiple concurrent viral outbreaks across China, including COVID-19, influenza A(H1N1), influenza B, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and rhinovirus, with COVID-19 linked to increasing heart attack cases. Hong Kong reportedly saw three COVID-19 deaths (ages 7, 9, and 12); Mainland China deaths were noted but not reported due to information suppression. No imported/exported cases were described.

triage.headline_ja: 北京の芸能マネージャー・郝泊言氏、新型コロナウイルス感染症で死去、享年39歳

triage.notes: 記事は著名人の死亡を契機に、中国本土および香港における複数の呼吸器系ウイルス（COVID-19、H1N1、インフルエンザB、RSV、ライノウイルス）の同時流行と、死亡者数の情報隠蔽疑惑を報じている。香港での小児死亡例（7・9・12歳）も言及されており、続報・公式統計の確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Cara Pemkab Kutai Timur Percepat Penanggulangan Penyakit TBC, Skrining 11 Ribu Lebih Warga
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: How the East Kutai Regency Government Accelerates TB Control, Screening More Than 11,000 Residents
article.articleSummary: East Kutai Regency's Health Office is accelerating TB control by prioritizing early detection to break transmission chains. Supported by the Ministry of Health, the program operates 118 screening loci, each screening 100 residents (about 11,800 people). Mobile X-ray units are deployed to sub-districts to enable field TB screening without hospital visits. If a resident tests positive, contact tracing extends to surrounding households to identify and test close contacts, with confirmed cases promptly entering standard treatment. The initiative supports the national target of TB elimination by 2030. Yuwana Sri Kurniawati, head of the Kutai Timur Health Office, emphasizes accessible, community-based screening to reach residents in remote areas. This report is current as of 11 November 2026.
