article.articleHeadline: Brasil confirma 5º foco da Doença de Newcastle
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Brazil confirms fifth outbreak of Newcastle disease.
article.articleSummary: Newcastle disease outbreak confirmed in Nova Itaberaba, Santa Catarina, Brazil, according to the Ministry of Agriculture. This marks the fifth documented focus in the region since Brazil declared a zoosanitary emergency last month. The repeated detections come from the same catarinense area; no laboratory-confirmed case counts or fatalities are provided in the report. Despite ongoing outbreaks, the business impact on Brazilian poultry exports has been limited because importing countries are regionalizing restrictions to the infected area rather than banning shipments from the country as a whole. The poultry sector, represented by ABPA, notes October exports of chicken meat rose, even as some embargoes were imposed due to the disease. The report highlights ongoing regionalized responses and the comparatively modest effect on international trade to date.

triage.headline_ja: ブラジル、ニューカッスル病の第5発生地を確認
triage.triage_reason: 動物感染症（ニューカッスル病）で人への健康影響はないが、ブラジルの家禽産業における繰り返しの発生と貿易制限の動きがあるため、今後の拡大・貿易影響を注視する必要がある。
triage.notes: 本疾患は動物（家禽）における感染症であり、ヒトへの公衆衛生リスクは報告されていない。貿易面では地域限定的な規制にとどまり、国全体への影響は限定的とされる。

article.articleHeadline: Karantina Babel periksa 149 sapi cegah tuberkulosis
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Babel quarantine checks 149 cattle to prevent tuberculosis.
article.articleSummary: 149 cattle were health-checked by the Bangka Belitung Islands quarantine office to detect Bovine Mycobacterium tuberculosis Complex (MTBC) as part of preventing bovine tuberculosis among farmers' cattle across Pangkalpinang City, Bangka Regency, Bangka Tengah, Bangka Barat, Bangka Selatan, Belitung, and Belitung Timur from September to early November 2026. Through intradermal comparative tuberculin testing with purified protein derivatives (PPD) avian and bovine, 0.1 mL per site, results showed no positive MTBC reactions after 72 hours. TB in cattle is chronic, reduces growth and productivity, and is a zoonosis risk via direct contact or consumption of contaminated animal products. This program strengthens intersectoral health surveillance, safeguards livestock movement, and supports farming in the Bangka Belitung Islands, with ongoing coordination with regional governments and agencies.

triage.headline_ja: バベル検疫局、牛結核症予防のため牛149頭を検査
triage.triage_reason: 検査の結果すべて陰性であり、ヒトまたは動物における実際の感染拡大は確認されていないため、通常の予防的サーベイランス活動として見送り。
triage.notes: 検査結果は全て陰性(MTBC非検出)であり、予防的な家畜検疫活動の報告。人への感染事例やアウトブレイクの記載はない。

article.articleHeadline: Benarkah Ruam Cacar Api yang Menyambung di Tengah Tanda Kematian?
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Is the confluent smallpox rash merging amid signs of death?
article.articleSummary: Shingles, caused by reactivation of varicella-zoster virus, can trigger a painful rash and long-lasting nerve pain. Debunking a myth, rashes meeting in the middle do not signal death, per Dr. Donnie Lumban Gaol at a Talkshow on Shingles for Kidney Disease Patients organized by KPCDI in South Jakarta on 8 Nov 2026. Mortality is linked to infection severity and complications, not rash convergence. Some patients experience intense, burn-like pain requiring prolonged care. Shingles can cause postherpetic neuralgia (persistent nerve pain for months or years) and other complications such as eye disorders, encephalitis, pneumonia, and vascular issues. Immunocompromised individuals, including chronic kidney disease patients on dialysis or kidney transplant recipients, require heightened monitoring. Disease progression typically: pain/itching 1–3 days; rash and blisters 4–8 days; crusting by weeks 2–4, with possible lingering neuropathic pain. Early medical consultation is advised.

triage.headline_ja: 帯状疱疹の発疹が中央で繋がると死の兆候というのは本当か？
triage.triage_reason: 個別の帯状疱疹に関する健康啓発・都市伝説否定の記事であり、公衆衛生上の緊急性や異常な流行を示す内容ではない。
triage.notes: 記事は帯状疱疹（水痘帯状疱疹ウイルスの再活性化）に関する一般向け健康教育・誤解の訂正を目的としたもので、アウトブレイクや公衆衛生上の脅威を示す情報ではない。

article.articleHeadline: RD Congo supera os 11 mil casos de ebola registrados
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: DR Congo surpasses 11,000 registered Ebola cases.
article.articleSummary: Democratic Republic of the Congo reports its worst Ebola outbreak on record, with 11,042 infections and 5,387 deaths, according to health authorities cited by AFP on 11 November 2026. The mid-May-declared outbreak is centered in eastern DRC amid armed conflict and weak state capacity, though cases have also appeared in Uganda, Kenya and Nigeria. The Bundibugyo strain remains a major barrier due to the lack of a variant-specific vaccine. Ervebo is approved only for the Zaire strain, and in October the World Health Organization began a regional clinical trial to assess its effectiveness. Médecins Sans Frontières urged rapid expansion of vaccine access for at-risk populations. In context, the 2018–2020 outbreak in DRC caused about 3,500 cases and 2,300 deaths, highlighting the current surge’s severity.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国、エボラ症例が1万1000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: 史上最悪規模のエボラ流行（死亡率約49%）で、武力紛争下での対応困難、ワクチン未対応株の拡大、複数国への越境拡大が確認されており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルRRAへ進むべき。
triage.notes: Uganda、Kenya、Nigeriaでも症例確認が報告されているが、対象国GeoNamesリストに含まれないためverified_locationsには含めていない。Bundibugyo株に対する承認済みワクチンが存在せず、WHOによる地域臨床試験が10月に開始された点が特筆される。

article.articleHeadline: O nouă variantă COVID-19, identificată în mai multe țări. Simptomele PJ.2.1 care pot fi confundate ușor cu o simplă răceală
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: A new COVID-19 variant identified in several countries. The PJ.2.1 symptoms that can be easily confused with a simple cold.
article.articleSummary: As of 11 November 2026, PJ.2.1, a new SARS-CoV-2 variant identified in multiple countries, was first detected May 2, 2026 in Ontario, Canada, with reports across other Canadian provinces and a US case in New York on June 30, 2026. It has since been reported in Australia, France, Spain, and other states. Early data show rapid spread but no evidence that PJ.2.1 causes more severe COVID-19 than prior variants. Genetic analyses focus on Spike protein mutations potentially affecting ACE2 interaction. Clinically, PJ.2.1 presents with non-specific symptoms overlapping influenza and other COVID-19 variants; common manifestations include fever or chills, cough, sore throat, nasal congestion, headache, myalgia, fatigue, dyspnea, digestive issues, and altered smell or taste. WHO notes symptoms alone cannot distinguish COVID-19 from influenza; testing guides diagnosis and treatment. No confirmed PJ.2.1 evidence in India; INSACOG monitors genetic changes.

triage.headline_ja: 新たなCOVID-19変異株が複数国で確認。単なる風邪と間違えやすいPJ.2.1の症状
triage.triage_reason: 新変異株PJ.2.1が複数国で検出され急速な拡大傾向があるが、重症度の増加は確認されておらず、対象国（インド）では確認事例がないため、国際的動向として経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 記事はカナダ・米国・フランス・オーストラリア・スペインでの検出を報告しているが、いずれも対象国リストに含まれない。インドについては『PJ.2.1の確認事例なし、INSACOGが監視中』と明記されており、対象国としての該当なしと判断した。

article.articleHeadline: أكثر من 11 ألف إصابة بالإيبولا في الكونغو.. كيف تستعد إفريقيا لمواجهة التفشي؟ | أهل مصر
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: More than 11,000 Ebola cases in Congo... How is Africa preparing to confront the outbreak?
article.articleSummary: As of 11 November 2026, Ebola virus disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 11,000 confirmed cases (11,042) and 5,387 deaths, making it the deadliest outbreak in the DRC and the second-largest globally after West Africa’s 2014–2016 epidemic. World Health Organization data through 3 November show 10,668 cases and 5,198 deaths, with transmission in eight provinces and 51 of 67 affected zones. The outbreak has raised cross-border concerns into other African countries, underscoring the need for regional surveillance. A 518-million-dollar continental plan by WHO and Africa CDC aims to bolster surveillance, laboratories, infection control, health workforce, and cross-border response in 10 priority countries (June–November 2026). The outbreak involves the Bundibugyo Ebola strain, for which no licensed vaccine or targeted therapy exists; two vaccine trials were approved, with initial results expected in 2027. Challenges include insecurity, limited access, weak infrastructure, misinformation, distrust, and deaths outside treatment centers.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴで1万1000人以上がエボラに感染…アフリカはどのように流行対策を進めているか
triage.triage_reason: DRCにおけるエボラ出血熱（ブンディブギョ株）が11,000例・死者5,387人を超え、過去最大級の規模に拡大。複数州・越境感染リスクがあり、WHO/Africa CDCが5.18億ドル規模の大陸対応計画を発動しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルRRAへ進むべき事案。
triage.notes: Angolaはサマリー上で主題として明示されておらず（越境懸念の一般的言及のみ）、対象国リストにも含まれないため除外。African大陸は国ではないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: Епидемията от ебола в Конго надхвърли 11 000 заразени и 5300 починали
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola outbreak in Congo surpassed 11,000 infections and 5,300 deaths.
article.articleSummary: As of 11 November 2026, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has infected 11,042 people and taken 5,387 lives, making it the deadliest Ebola outbreak in the country’s history and the second-largest globally after West Africa’s 2014–2016 epidemic (more than 28,600 cases and over 11,000 deaths). Delayed detection, armed conflict, and an overwhelmed health system have fueled faster spread than previous outbreaks. The disease is now established across Eastern, Central, and Western Africa, making this the widest African outbreak of Ebola to date, according to the Associated Press.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ流行、感染者1万1000人、死者5300人を超える
triage.triage_reason: DRCにおけるエボラ流行が国内史上最悪規模（感染1万1042人、死亡5387人）に達し、致死率も高く、複数地域に拡大しているためIHR基準・WPRO基準の双方で複数該当する。
triage.notes: 記事はAP通信の報道を引用し、DRC国内史上最悪のエボラ流行であり、武力紛争や医療システムの崩壊が拡大要因とされている。アンゴラは発生地域に含まれるが、記事本文で主題として扱われていないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: Acute Pulmonary Embolism May Complicate Tracheobronchial Tuberculosis
article.articleSummary: Five consecutive adults undergoing active anti-tuberculosis treatment for tracheobronchial tuberculosis at Tianjin Haihe Hospital and affiliated institutes in Tianjin, China, were diagnosed with acute pulmonary embolism (PE) between December 2023 and August 2025. CT pulmonary angiography confirmed PE in all cases. Tracheobronchial TB was diagnosed via imaging, bronchoscopy/pathology, and microbiological evidence of Mycobacterium tuberculosis. The cohort’s mean age was 77 years; four were women and one man. PE onset occurred 7–114 days after TB diagnosis (mean 51 days) and all events happened during anti-TB therapy. Symptoms were predominantly progressive dyspnea; classical chest pain, hemoptysis, fever, and marked hypoxemia were uncommon. D-dimer was universally elevated; inflammatory and cardiac injury markers were not consistently abnormal. CT showed varied clot distributions: bilateral multiple emboli in three patients, isolated left in one, and right in one. Anticoagulation therapy was used as part of management.

triage.headline_ja: 急性肺塞栓症が気管支結核治療中に合併する可能性
triage.triage_reason: 単一医療機関における症例シリーズ報告（臨床研究）であり、公衆衛生上の異常事態や国際的拡大リスク、社会的関心の高まりを示す要素がない。
triage.notes: 本記事は結核治療中の合併症（肺塞栓症）に関する臨床研究報告であり、感染症アウトブレイクや公衆衛生危機の兆候ではない。

article.articleHeadline: Kenya's Last Ebola Patient Goes Home
article.articleSummary: Kenya’s final Ebola patient was discharged on 11 November 2026, as the country begins a 42‑day countdown to determine if the outbreak is officially over. The Health Ministry reports nine confirmed cases, all from a single imported infection, with two deaths; seven patients recovered. The last new Kenyan case was confirmed 19 October 2026. Contacts (135 people) completed 21 days of monitoring before the final discharge. If no new case emerges by 23 December 2026, Kenya may be declared Ebola-free; a new case would restart the clock. Kenya will keep screening at 26 entry points and maintain rapid response teams. An upcoming advisory for Kenyans returning from Congo will require a health declaration via the OHAI chatbot, on‑arrival screening, and 21 days of follow‑up. Kenya will not issue Ebola‑free certificates or act as a quarantine hub; the Congo outbreak persists with >11,000 cases.

triage.headline_ja: ケニアの最後のエボラ患者が退院
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱は重篤な疾患であり、ケニアでの輸入症例の発生とコンゴ(DRC)での1万1000例を超える継続的な大規模流行が報告されているため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はケニアにおける輸入エボラ症例の終息（42日間のカウントダウン開始）だが、感染源であるコンゴ民主共和国（DRC）では1万1000例を超える大規模流行が継続中であり、対象国リストに含まれるDRCのみをverified_locationsに記載した。ケニアは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。

locations.name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

article.articleHeadline: Major virus warnings as 2 deadly diseases spread globally - and one may be in UK
article.articleSummary: Two simultaneous threats: Aedes aegypti, the dengue/yellow fever mosquito, was found breeding at homes in east London, the first record of the species in the UK. UKHSA has enhanced surveillance, begun larval control, and says the public risk remains very low with no evidence of human infections and no detections in nearby public areas. Separately, Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD), an Ebola-related outbreak, is expanding in the Democratic Republic of the Congo with sustained high transmission; WHO reported 512 deaths since 21 October (335 in communities, 177 in treatment centres). One confirmed BVD case has been identified in the United Kingdom, with Switzerland and the UK previously medically evacuated confirmed cases from the DRC. On 5 November 2026, the UK evacuated one confirmed case, now in London. No new cases in Kenya or Nigeria; no travel restrictions advised.

triage.headline_ja: 世界的に拡大する2つの危険な感染症に関する重大な警告 - 一方は英国内に存在する可能性
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのブンディブギョウイルス病（エボラ関連）アウトブレイクが持続的に高い感染拡大を示し、死者512名、英国・スイスへの国際的な症例拡大が確認されているため、フルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: ネッタイシマカの英国内発見は別事案として報告されているが人への感染例なしで公衆衛生リスクは低いとされている。主要な懸念はDRCのブンディブギョウイルス病アウトブレイクであり、英国・スイスへの輸入症例（医療搬送）が確認されている。ケニア・ナイジェリアでは新規症例なし。

article.articleHeadline: 민주콩고 에볼라 확진자 1만1천명 넘어...보름 새 1천명 증가
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola confirmed cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo exceed 11,000, up 1,000 in two weeks.
article.articleSummary: DRC Ebola outbreak surpasses 11,000 cases; as of 9 November 2026, INSP reports 11,042 cumulative Ebola cases, up about 1,000 in two weeks. Death toll 5,387 (case fatality rate 48.8%); recoveries 2,990, with 973 currently in treatment. The prevailing outbreak is Bundibugyo ebolavirus in eastern provinces Ituri and North Kivu. No approved vaccine or therapy exists for Bundibugyo, but the Ervebo vaccine (for Zaire ebolavirus) has shown some beneficial effects in animal studies and began vaccination of residents and healthcare workers on 26 August; 21,866 people have been vaccinated to date. Ongoing containment challenges include armed conflict, distrust, misinformation, violence against health workers, and wage arrears causing strikes at clinics and checkpoints. Kenya aims to declare ends after six weeks without new cases; Uganda’s co-epidemic was declared over last August; Nigeria reports one imported case (Swiss citizen) with no further transmission. Current date used: 2026-11-11.

triage.headline_ja: 民主コンゴのエボラ確定症例、1万1千人を超える…2週間で1千人増加
triage.triage_reason: 致死率約49%、1万人超の大規模アウトブレイクで承認されたワクチン・治療法が存在せず、武装紛争や医療従事者への暴力など対応困難要因が継続しており、国際的拡大（ナイジェリア輸入例）も確認されているためフルRRAが必要。
triage.notes: ナイジェリア・ケニア・ウガンダは関連国として言及されているが、主たる流行地はDRC東部（イトゥリ・北キブ）であり、対象国リストに含まれるのはDRCのみ。ナイジェリアの輸入症例はそれ以上の伝播なしと報告。

article.articleHeadline: Eμπολα: Ξεπέρασαν τις 11.000 τα κρούσματα στη ΛΔ Κονγκό - Εξιτήριο για τον τελευταίο ασθενή στην Κένυα
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola: The number of cases in the DRC exceeded 11,000 — Discharge for the last patient in Kenya.
article.articleSummary: As of 11 November 2026, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has 11,042 cases and 5,387 deaths, with about 2,990 recoveries (case-fatality rate 48.8%). Declared mid-May, it is the country’s 17th outbreak, originating in Ituri and spreading to seven provinces, mainly Ituri and North Kivu, with cross-border cases in Uganda, Kenya, and Nigeria. Violence hampers response: a health center in Ituri was burned; Fataki clashes paused health activities; ADF attacks have hit Ituri, Haut Uele, and North Kivu. Bundibugyo strain drives this outbreak; no approved vaccine for Bundibugyo. MSF urges wider Ervebo access; WHO began a clinical trial in the DRC to test Ervebo against Bundibugyo. In Kenya, the last patient was discharged on 11 November, launching a 42-day monitoring period; nine cases total (two deaths, seven recoveries), no new infections since 19 October, and 11 contacts completed quarantine; entrants from DRC face a 21-day quarantine.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱：DRCの症例数が11,000人を超える―ケニアの最後の患者が退院
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ出血熱アウトブレイクが11,000例超・致死率48.8%に達し、複数国への越境拡大、ワクチン未承認株、紛争による対応阻害など複数のIHR基準・WPRO基準に該当するため。
triage.notes: ケニア・ウガンダ・ナイジェリアへの越境症例が報告されているが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsから除外。DRCが主題であり、Bundibugyo株に対する承認ワクチンがない点、武力紛争による対応阻害が深刻なリスク要因。

article.articleHeadline: Έμπολα: Περισσότερα από 11.000 κρούσματα έχουν καταγραφεί στη ΛΔ Κονγκό - Εξιτήριο πήρε ο τελευταίος ασθενής στην Κένυα
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola: More than 11,000 cases have been recorded in the Democratic Republic of the Congo - the last patient in Kenya has been discharged.
article.articleSummary: Ebola: Democratic Republic of Congo reports 11,042 cases and 5,387 deaths from the Bundibugyo strain outbreak, with about 2,990 recoveries; case fatality 48.8% per INSP. The 17th Ebola outbreak in DRC began in Ituri (northeast) and spread to seven other provinces, with Ituri and North Kivu bearing most cases. Cross-border spillovers have reached Uganda, Kenya, and Nigeria. No vaccine exists for Bundibugyo; MSF calls for expanded access to Ervebo (Zaire strain) to protect vulnerable groups. WHO began a clinical trial in DRC on Oct 24 to assess cross-protection against Bundibugyo. Violence in Ituri, including attacks on health centers, hampers response. Kenya today discharged the last Ebola patient, starting a 42-day countdown to end the outbreak there; Kenya recorded nine cases (all linked to the index case), one death, and seven recoveries. Contacts were released; entrants from DRC face a 21-day quarantine.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱：コンゴ民主共和国で11,000例以上を記録、ケニアで最後の患者が退院
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ（ブンディブギョ株）アウトブレイクは致死率48.8%、11,042症例・5,387死亡に達し、既にウガンダ・ケニア・ナイジェリアへの国際的拡大が確認されている。ワクチン未承認・武力紛争による対応困難も重なり、フルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 記事はDRC（イトゥリ州発生、7州に拡大）が主題。ウガンダ・ケニア・ナイジェリアへの越境拡大も記載されているが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsから除外。ケニアでの最後の患者退院は収束に向けた進展を示すが、DRC本体の流行は継続中。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola já matou 5.387 pessoas em surto no Congo
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola has already killed 5,387 people in an outbreak in the Congo.
article.articleSummary: As of November 11, 2026, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has reached 11,042 cases and 5,387 deaths, according to the Ministry of Health. It is the deadliest Ebola outbreak recorded in the country, with spread to eight of the 26 provinces. The Bundibugyo ebolavirus (Bundibugyo virus) is identified as the causative agent. There is no vaccine or approved treatment for Bundibugyo virus. The outbreak was declared in mid-May, and ongoing conflict and a strained health system hinder containment and response efforts.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでのエボラ流行、死者5,387人に
triage.triage_reason: DRCで過去最悪規模のエボラ流行（11,042症例、死者5,387人）が8州に拡大し、ワクチン・治療法のないブンディブギョ株であること、紛争により対応が困難な状況であり、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するため。
triage.notes: ワクチン・承認された治療法がないブンディブギョ株であること、紛争により保健システムが脆弱な状況下での封じ込めが困難である点が特に懸念される。

article.articleHeadline: Covid-19: BH registra maior índice de testes positivos em 2026
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: COVID-19: Belo Horizonte records the highest positivity rate in 2026.
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 in Belo Horizonte, Minas Gerais, Brazil shows 7% test positivity in the week of 25–31 Oct 2026—the highest for 2026, up from 1% at the start of October. The city records 27,885 suspected COVID-19 cases, 449 confirmed cases, and nine deaths in 2026, eight of whom were 60 years or older. The rise aligns with broader increases in respiratory illnesses; Fiocruz InfoGripe notes rising Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome cases nationwide, including COVID-19. Vaccination remains the primary prevention under the National Immunization Calendar for elderly (60+), children 6 months–under 5 years, pregnant individuals, health workers, and other priority groups; vaccination sites are listed on the city portal. Common symptoms include fever, chills, cough, fatigue, dyspnea, myalgias, headache, sore throat, congestion, plus possible GI symptoms. Preventive measures include vaccination, masking indoors, hand hygiene, ventilation, and reducing contact when symptomatic. InfoGripe reports 75% growth probability in Maranhão, Piauí, and Roraima; 95% in Minas Gerais and many other states.

triage.headline_ja: COVID-19：ベロオリゾンテで2026年最多の陽性率を記録
triage.triage_reason: 季節性のCOVID-19増加を示す通常の公衆衛生モニタリング情報であり、重症度や国際的拡大の証拠は乏しいが、複数州での増加傾向があるため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 既知の病原体（COVID-19）の季節的増加であり、死亡者は9名（うち8名が60歳以上）と重症度は限定的。国内の複数州（Minas Gerais, Maranhão, Piauí, Roraima）で感染増加の兆候があるが、国際的な拡大や渡航制限のリスクは報告されていない。

article.articleHeadline: Veterinary students become agents of change in fight against rabies
article.articleSummary: Nearly 500 students and lecturers at the Veterinary Medicine Faculty of the Vietnam National University of Agriculture (VNUA) in Hà Nội were trained on rabies prevention by SBCC Vietnam and the Soi Dog Foundation, to become ambassadors for behavioural change. The program supports Vietnam’s goal of zero human rabies deaths by 2030, aligned with WHO strategy, noting that rabies is almost always fatal once symptoms appear but preventable. It highlights the transmission chain from the dog and cat meat trade to humans. Hanoi approved in July 2025 a project: Pilot Model for Rabies Prevention and Sustainable Economic Development—phased transition of the dog and cat meat trade in selected wards—a three-stage plan: vocational training, startup assistance and market links. The initiative will involve 14 pilot wards across Hà Nội, with student ambassadors turning scientific knowledge into community action under a One Health approach.

triage.headline_ja: 獣医学生たちが狂犬病撲滅運動の変革の担い手に
triage.triage_reason: 狂犬病啓発・教育プログラムに関する内容であり、新規症例報告やアウトブレイクではなく、公衆衛生上の緊急性や異常性は認められない。
triage.notes: 本記事はハノイにおける狂犬病予防教育・犬猫肉取引の段階的転換プロジェクトに関する内容であり、具体的な感染事例やアウトブレイクの報告ではない。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola : en RDC, principal foyer de l'épidémie, plus de 11000 cas recensés
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola: in the DRC, the outbreak's epicenter, more than 11,000 cases recorded.
article.articleSummary: Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo continues to surge, with authorities reporting 11,042 cases and 5,387 deaths as of November 11, 2026. Kinshasa confirms the outbreak is the largest in the country’s history and remains active across the DRC. The World Health Organization has warned about the spread of the Bundibugyo strain, for which there is no vaccine or approved treatment. The Associated Press, citing the Congolese Ministry of Health, notes that the death toll is nearing half of total infections, underscoring the severity and sustained transmission of the ongoing epidemic in the DRC. The Bundibugyo strain's lack of vaccine or treatment poses containment challenges.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱：DRCにおいて、流行の中心地で11,000例以上の症例が記録される
triage.triage_reason: DRCでエボラ(ブンディブギョ株)が史上最大規模で拡大し、致死率も高く、ワクチン・治療薬が存在しないため国際的拡大・公衆衛生リスクともに深刻でIHR基準を複数満たす。
triage.notes: ブンディブギョ株による大規模流行で致死率約49%、ワクチン・治療法未確立のため国際支援ニーズが高い。

article.articleHeadline: Kenya Begins 42-Day Countdown towards Ebola-free Status after discharging last patient
article.articleSummary: Kenya begins a 42-day countdown toward Ebola-free status after discharging the last Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) patient in Nairobi on Nov 11, 2026. The countdown starts Nov 12; if no new infections are reported, the declaration is expected around Dec 23, 2026. Seven recoveries and two deaths occurred among nine confirmed cases, all linked to a single transmission cluster; eight secondary infections involved four family members and four healthcare workers. The outbreak began with an imported case confirmed Oct 6, 2026, in a Kenyan who traveled from the DRC via Uganda; the patient died Oct 5 and was buried under Ebola protocols. Last confirmed infection was Oct 19, per WHO. The response emphasized surveillance, isolation, contact tracing, and entry-point screening. By Oct 6, 652,000 travellers were screened; 267 samples tested; 5,000+ health workers trained. Lab confirmation: National Virology Reference Laboratory and KEMRI; WHO/Africa CDC provided support.

triage.headline_ja: ケニア、最後の患者退院後にエボラフリー認定に向けた42日間のカウントダウンを開始
triage.triage_reason: エボラ（ブンディブギョウイルス病）のアウトブレイクで死亡例・医療従事者感染・国境を越えた伝播（DRC→ウガンダ→ケニア）が確認されており、IHR基準に複数該当するためフルRRA対象とする。
triage.notes: 本イベントはケニア（対象国リスト外）で発生したエボラ（BVD）アウトブレイクであり、輸入症例の起点とされるDRCは記事の主題ではないため verified_locations には含めない。ケニア国内での二次感染・医療従事者感染が確認されており、WHO/Africa CDCが支援。アウトブレイクは収束傾向にあり、42日間の監視期間終了後にエボラフリー宣言が見込まれる。

article.articleHeadline: اخبارك نت | عدد مصابي "إيبولا" في الكونغو يتجاوز 11 ألفا
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Akhbarak.net | The number of Ebola cases in the Congo surpasses 11,000.
article.articleSummary: Confirmed Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of Congo exceed 11,000, with 11,042 confirmed cases and 5,387 deaths reported as of November 11, 2026. The outbreak is driven by the rare Bundibugyo strain, for which there is no approved treatment or vaccine. It began in mid-May and constitutes the second-largest and deadliest Ebola outbreak on record, after West Africa’s 2014–2016 epidemic (over 28,000 infections and more than 11,000 deaths). Eight of the DRC’s 26 provinces have been affected, with many fatalities occurring outside treatment centers. Delays in detection, ongoing conflict, and strained health services have accelerated spread compared with prior outbreaks. The outbreak now spans East, Central, and West Africa, marking the most geographically widespread Ebola outbreak on the continent to date.

triage.headline_ja: アクバラク・ネット｜コンゴのエボラ感染者数が1万1000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: DRCで11,042例・5,387人死亡という大規模流行で、治療薬・ワクチンのない希少株による史上2番目に大きいエボラ流行であり、広域拡散・医療逼迫を伴うためIHR基準を複数満たす。
triage.notes: 発生地域にMozambique、Angolaが含まれるが、記事サマリーはDRC国内の流行拡大（8/26州）を述べており、他国への越境拡大の明記はないため対象外とした。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola-Epidemie im Kongo: Zahl der Infektionsfälle auf über 11.000 gestiegen
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola epidemic in the Congo: the number of infections has risen to over 11,000.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo exceeds 11,000 infections, with 11,042 cases and 5,387 deaths reported by the National Health Institute; about 3,000 patients have recovered. The mid-May outbreak is the worst in the country’s history, and experts believe the virus circulated undetected for months prior to confirmation. The Bundibugyo variant is responsible; unlike the Zaire variant, there is currently no licensed vaccine or approved treatment, though several therapeutics are in trials. Transmission occurs via direct contact with bodily fluids, causing fever, muscle pains, diarrhea, internal bleeding, and organ failure. Infections have also been detected in Kenya, Nigeria, and Uganda, indicating cross-border spread. Ongoing public health responses monitor transmissions and enforce containment measures across affected regions.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ流行：感染者数が11,000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ流行は感染者11,000人超・死者5,387人と深刻で、ワクチン未承認のブンディブギョ株による国境を越えた拡大（ケニア・ナイジェリア・ウガンダ）が報告されており、IHR基準に複数該当する。
triage.notes: 記事ではケニア・ナイジェリア・ウガンダへの感染拡大も言及されているが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsから除外。DRCが主たる発生地域であり、国境を越えた拡大傾向は重要な懸念材料。ブンディブギョ変異株にはワクチン・承認治療薬が存在しない点も重症度・管理可能性の懸念を高めている。

article.articleHeadline: Sốt xuất huyết diễn biến nặng, bác sĩ cảnh báo dấu hiệu nguy hiểm
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Dengue fever progresses to a severe stage; doctors warn of dangerous signs.
article.articleSummary: Dengue fever cases in Vietnam progressed to severe dengue at the National Hospital for Tropical Diseases in Hanoi. Two patients, a 53-year-old woman from Hai Phong and a 23-year-old woman from Hanoi, developed dengue with liver injury and coagulation disturbances. Platelets fell to 21–23 x10^9/L, with AST elevations near 1,900 U/L and ALT around 804–883 U/L; ultrasound showed ascites and bilateral pleural effusions, indicating plasma leakage. Both were diagnosed with severe dengue and require close monitoring for hemorrhage, circulatory disturbance, and other complications. The hospital is treating 16 dengue patients, with some in severe condition. Dengue is transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes; platelet count alone does not determine severity. Severe dengue often emerges during days 3–7 of illness. Guidance emphasizes seeking prompt care for abdominal pain, vomiting, bleeding, or dehydration, avoiding NSAIDs, staying hydrated, vector control, and vaccination considerations.

triage.headline_ja: デング熱重症化、医師が危険兆候を警告
triage.triage_reason: ベトナムでデング熱重症例が複数報告されているが、デング熱自体は同地域で季節的に流行する既知の疾患であり、現時点では個別医療機関の症例報告にとどまるため、続報を注視する段階と判断。
triage.notes: デング熱はベトナムの風土病的疾患であり毎年流行が見られる。本記事は特定病院での重症例の臨床報告が中心で、大規模アウトブレイクや異常な拡大を示す情報はない。季節的増加や重症例数の推移について続報を要観察。

article.articleHeadline: Deadliest Ebola outbreak in Congo's history reaches 11,000 cases
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-11-11, Congo's Ebola outbreak has reached 11,042 cases and 5,387 deaths, the deadliest and fastest-growing in the country's history. The Bundibugyo virus outbreak, the 17th in Congo, declared in May, centers in Ituri and North Kivu and remains hard to control amid armed conflict, health-system crisis, poor roads, and violence fueled by mistrust. Unpaid salaries and strikes have paralysed facilities and disrupted screening at transport hubs, rivers, borders and airports. Mistrust, rumours, and resistance to safe burials, along with reduced attendance at health facilities, hinder containment. There is no approved vaccine yet; however, two candidates backed by WHO—Oxford University with the Serum Institute of India, and Moderna—are entering trials led by the DRC's National Institute for Biomedical Research with international partners. The outbreak surpassed 1,000 cases within 40 days of response activation, far faster than the 2018 outbreak (235 days).

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ史上最悪のエボラ出血熱アウトブレイク、1万1000例に到達
triage.triage_reason: 致死率の高いエボラ（Bundibugyoウイルス）の大規模アウトブレイクであり、死者数・感染拡大速度、医療崩壊、国際的支援（ワクチン治験）の必要性など複数基準に該当するため。
triage.notes: イトゥリ州・北キブ州を中心にコンゴ国内で発生。承認済みワクチンがなく、国際機関（WHO、オックスフォード大学/セラムインスティテュート、モデルナ）が治験に関与しており、国際的な支援ニーズが明確。

article.articleHeadline: آخر مصاب بالإيبولا يغادر المستشفى في كينيا.. وبدء العدّ التنازلي لإعلان خلوّها من المرض
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The last Ebola patient leaves the hospital in Kenya, and the countdown to declaring it Ebola-free has begun.
article.articleSummary: As of 11 November 2026, Kenya has discharged its last Ebola patient, beginning a 42-day countdown to declare the country Ebola-free. Nine Ebola virus disease cases have been recorded in Kenya since early October, all linked to the index patient who arrived from the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and died after arrival. The remaining infections were among the index case's contacts; one of them died and seven recovered. No new cases have been reported since 19 October, and the final 11 contacts completed quarantine and were discharged on Wednesday. Kenya will impose a 21-day quarantine for travelers arriving from the DRC as part of preventive measures. The broader Ebola outbreak is now spreading across four African countries in East, Central, and West Africa, with the DRC outbreak as the second-largest on record, exceeding 11,000 confirmed cases.

triage.headline_ja: ケニアで最後のエボラ患者が退院、エボラ終息宣言へのカウントダウン開始
triage.triage_reason: DRCで発生中のエボラ流行は過去2番目の規模（1万1千例超）でアフリカ4カ国に拡大しており、ケニアへの越境感染例・渡航制限措置も発生しているためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: ケニアは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations から除外。DRCの流行が主題であり継続注視が必要。アフリカ4カ国への拡大の詳細国名は記事に明記されていないため不明。

article.articleHeadline: Kenya Begins 42-Day Countdown to Ebola-Free Status After All Patients Discharged
article.articleSummary: Kenya's Ebola response moves to final monitoring after the last confirmed patient was discharged on 11 November 2026, sealing a nine-case, single-transmission cluster first detected as an imported infection on 6 October. With no patients under care, a 42-day countdown toward an Ebola-free status begins, aiming for 23 December 2026 if no new cases emerge. Authorities report zero community transmission, and all 135 contacts traced have completed follow-up with none remaining in quarantine. Surveillance continues, rapid-response teams stay on alert, and entry-point screening remains active. An advisory for travelers from Ebola-affected areas, notably the Democratic Republic of Congo, includes pre-travel health declarations via the OHAI chatbot, on-arrival screening, and 21-day health follow-up. Kenya will not quarantine foreign nationals or issue Ebola-free certificates for travel and urges other countries to lift travel restrictions. No movement bans or gatherings restrictions are in place.

triage.headline_ja: ケニア、全患者退院後にエボラ出血熱終息へ向けた42日間のカウントダウンを開始
triage.triage_reason: ケニアで発生した輸入エボラ症例クラスター（9例）はすでに地域内感染ゼロ・接触者追跡完了という収束段階にあり、新規の公衆衛生脅威というよりは既存アウトブレイクの終息モニタリング報告であるため、フルRRAよりも経過観察が妥当と判断した。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はケニアにおけるエボラクラスターの終息プロセスであるが、ケニア（Kenya, geonames未対象国）は対象国リストに含まれないため除外。DRCは輸入元として言及されているのみで、現地発生の主題ではないが、エボラ流行継続国として参考情報として記載。実質的な現発生国はケニアであり、対象国リストに該当国なしの可能性が高い。

article.articleHeadline: Congo, più di 11mila casi di Ebola: sono oltre 5mila i morti
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Congo, more than 11,000 Ebola cases: over 5,000 deaths.
article.articleSummary: Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has reached 11,042 confirmed cases and 5,387 deaths, government data show. The outbreak, caused by the rare Bundibugyo variant of Ebola, was declared in mid-May. There are no approved treatments or vaccines for this variant. It ranks as the second most extensive and deadly Ebola outbreak in Africa, surpassed only by the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic that infected over 28,600 people and killed more than 11,000. Eight of the DRC’s 26 provinces have been affected, with many deaths occurring outside care facilities. Delayed diagnosis, ongoing conflict, and strained health services have accelerated spread. The disease has now been reported across East, Central, and West Africa, marking the widest geographic distribution for an Ebola outbreak on the continent to date.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ、エボラ出血熱症例が1万1000人超：死者5000人以上
triage.triage_reason: DRCでエボラ出血熱（まれなブンディブギョ株）が11,000例超・死者5,000人超に達し、アフリカ史上2番目に大規模な流行となっており、複数州・広範な地理的拡大が確認されているためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーではDRC国内（26州中8州）での流行拡大が述べられており、東・中央・西アフリカへの地理的拡大は言及されているが、モザンビークやアンゴラでの具体的な発生は記載されていないため対象国として含めていない。

article.articleHeadline: Вспышка Эболы в ДР Конго достигла 11 000 случаев и стала самой смертоносной
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in DR Congo has reached 11,000 cases and has become the deadliest.
article.articleSummary: DR Congo's Bundibugyo ebolavirus outbreak has reached 11,042 cases and 5,387 deaths, the deadliest in the country’s history. It is the 17th Ebola outbreak there and the fastest-spreading on record, with more than 1,000 confirmed cases within 40 days of response start (vs about 235 days in 2018). The epicenters are Ituri and North Kivu amid ongoing conflict, weak health systems, and distrust that hamper control efforts. Unpaid wages and strikes have paralyzed key facilities and disrupted checkpoints, ports, borders, and airports; renewed armed violence threatens access for clinicians. There is no approved vaccine or treatment yet; two candidate vaccines, Oxford University with Serum Institute of India and Moderna, are in trials led by INRB with WHO support, begun around November 4. Vaccines complement but do not replace surveillance, testing, isolation, safe burials, and trusted community engagement; the 2014-2016 West Africa outbreak caused over 11,000 deaths.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱流行が11,000例に達し、史上最悪の流行となった
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で史上最悪・最速拡大のエボラ出血熱流行が発生し、死者5,387人、ワクチン未承認で紛争地域のため対応が困難なため、フルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 発生地域にAngolaが含まれているが、記事サマリーではDRC（Ituri、North Kivu）のみが流行地として言及されており、Angolaでの症例報告はないため除外した。国境・空港の混乱が言及されているが、正式な渡航制限措置については記載がない。

article.articleHeadline: Ебола в Конго: заразените вече са над 11 000
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in Congo: the infected are already over 11,000.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has surpassed 11,000 cases, with 11,042 infections and 5,387 deaths as of 11 November 2026. The Bundibugyo ebolavirus strain driving the outbreak has no approved vaccine or specific treatment and has spread to eight of the country’s 26 provinces since it was declared in mid-May. Renewed violence in Ituri and North Kivu is hampering response efforts, with attacks on health facilities and workers amid distrust and misinformation. The outbreak has extended to neighboring countries, including Uganda, Kenya, and Nigeria, prompting calls for ceasefires to enable access for responders and for intensified surveillance, rapid isolation, and protection of frontline staff to curb transmission.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ出血熱：感染者はすでに11,000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: 致死率の高いエボラ出血熱が11,000人超の感染・5,387人の死亡に拡大し、近隣国にも波及、紛争により対応が阻害されているためIHR基準を複数満たす。
triage.notes: ウガンダ・ケニア・ナイジェリアへの拡大が記載されているが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。紛争地域での対応困難が流行制御を一層難しくしている。

article.articleHeadline: Quênia dá alta ao último paciente de ebola e inicia contagem para ser declarado livre da doença
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Kenya discharges the last Ebola patient and begins the countdown to being declared disease-free.
article.articleSummary: Kenya discharged the last Ebola patient on 11 November 2026 and started a 42-day countdown to being declared free of the disease, with a deadline of 23 December 2026, equal to twice the virus’ longest incubation period. Nine Ebola cases were recorded in October, including two deaths. The initial patient, who traveled from Congo via Uganda, transmitted the virus to four family members and four health workers. Seven of the nine cases recovered; 135 contacts were traced. The Ministry of Health says all confirmed cases were linked to the initial patient’s contact list, indicating no community transmission. The Congo outbreak, centered in May and also impacting Uganda and Nigeria, reports 11,042 infections and 5,387 deaths. Kenya will maintain prevention measures, including border controls and a dedicated airport gate for passengers from ten high-risk countries. Saudi Arabia suspended Kenyan visa issuance on 30 October, affecting hundreds seeking Gulf work.

triage.headline_ja: ケニアが最後のエボラ患者を退院させ、疾病フリー宣言へ向けた42日間のカウントダウンを開始
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国（DRC）を起源とする大規模エボラ流行（11,042感染・5,387死亡）が継続しており、ウガンダ・ナイジェリア・ケニアへの越境伝播やサウジアラビアによるビザ発給停止など国際的な渡航制限が生じているため、フルリスク評価が必要と判断した。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はケニアでの流行終息とカウントダウン開始だが、背景として言及されるDRC（コンゴ民主共和国）起源の大規模流行（11,042感染・5,387死亡）が対象国リストに該当するため、これを主要評価対象とした。ケニア・ウガンダ・ナイジェリア・サウジアラビアは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations から除外した。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola-járvány Kongóban: 11 042 eset, a valaha volt leghalálosabb
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo: 11,042 cases, the deadliest on record.
article.articleSummary: 11,042 identified Ebola cases and 5,387 deaths in the Democratic Republic of the Congo—the deadliest outbreak in the country’s history—persist amid conflict, strikes and public mistrust. The outbreak, centered in Ituri and North Kivu, is the 17th in DRC and the fastest-spreading to date; within 40 days of the response, cases surpassed 1,000, far faster than the 2018 outbreak (about 235 days). Ongoing violence, deteriorating health infrastructure, disrupted transportation and unchecked misinformation hinder control efforts, with healthcare workers facing safety threats and clinics and checkpoints closed. No licensed vaccine exists, but two candidates are in trials: one from the University of Oxford and Serum Institute, and another from Moderna, coordinated by DRC’s National Biomedical Research Institute with WHO support. article.articleHeadline: В Кения бе изписан и последният пациент, заразен с ебола
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: In Kenya, the last patient infected with Ebola was discharged.
article.articleSummary: Kenya discharged the last Ebola patient, beginning a 42-day surveillance period to declare elimination if no new cases arise. The region's outbreak tally exceeds 11,000 cases since May in the Democratic Republic of Congo, with 5,387 deaths. In Kenya, nine new cases were reported in October; the index patient traveled from Congo via Uganda and spread to four relatives and four health workers. The mother died; the others recovered. Authorities tracked 135 contacts linked to the first patient. Kenya’s countdown ends December 23, but Health Minister Aden Duale says it doubles the incubation period and protections remain. Congo remains the epicenter (11,042 cases, 5,387 deaths); Uganda and Nigeria have reported cases via travelers. Kenya tightened border controls, established a special airport checkpoint for travelers from 10 at-risk countries, with thermal screening and health declarations; arrivals from the DRC face 21-day quarantine. Saudi Arabia suspended Kenyan visa issuance from Oct 30.

triage.headline_ja: ケニアでエボラに感染した最後の患者が退院

article.articleHeadline: RD Congo supera los 11.000 casos de ébola registrados Ensegundos República Dominicana
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: DR Congo surpasses 11,000 reported Ebola cases.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo surpasses 11,000 cases, marking the country’s worst on record. Declared mid-May after delays, the crisis concentrates in eastern DR Congo amid armed conflict, with spillover cases reported in Uganda, Kenya, and Nigeria. The Congolese National Institute of Public Health tallies 11,042 infections and 5,387 deaths. Transmission occurs via contact with bodily fluids, causing a severe hemorrhagic fever. The Bundibugyo strain is identified as the outbreak origin, for which there is no specific vaccine in local use; the World Health Organization began a clinical trial in October to test Ervebo, currently approved only for the Zaire strain. MSF has urged urgent expansion of vaccine access for those at risk. The 2018–2020 outbreak remains the most severe reference point, with far fewer cases and deaths.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国、エボラ出血熱の報告症例数が11,000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱が過去最悪規模(11,000例超、死者5,387人)に拡大し、武力紛争地域での流行かつウガンダ・ケニア・ナイジェリアへの越境例が報告されており、IHR基準の複数該当とWPRO基準も複数該当するため。

article.articleHeadline: Najgroźniejsza epidemia eboli w historii Konga: ponad 11 tys. zakażeń
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The deadliest Ebola epidemic in Congo's history: over 11,000 infections.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) now the deadliest in the country’s history, with 11,042 cases and 5,387 deaths, nearly half of confirmed infections. The 17th outbreak, the fastest-spreading to date, was officially declared in May and continues to expand. Ituri and North Kivu provinces are the epicenters; ongoing armed conflict, a collapsing health system, poor roads, and violence fueled by distrust and misinformation hinder response. Strikes and unpaid salaries disrupt health facilities, checkpoints, ports, borders, and airports, complicating access to care and surveillance. Distrust leads to refusals of testing and unsafe burials, undermining outbreak control. The culprit is Bundibugyo ebolavirus, for which there is no approved vaccine or treatment yet; WHO notes two vaccine candidates (Oxford University with Serum Institute of India, and Moderna) undergoing trials by INRB with international partners. WHO emphasizes proven measures—early care, contact tracing, isolation, safe burials, and community trust—as essential.

article.articleHeadline: Kenia da de alta a su último paciente de ébola tras registrar 23 días sin nuevos contagios
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Kenya Discharges Its Last Ebola Patient After Recording 23 Days Without New Infections.
article.articleSummary: Kenya discharged its last Ebola patient on 11 November 2026 after 23 days without new infections, launching a 42-day countdown to declare the country Ebola-free. Health Minister Aden Duale said there are no patients in treatment and no quarantined contacts, with 11 cleared after observation. The first Kenyan case was a 40-year-old man who spent seven days in the DRC before travelling to Kampala and Nairobi; he died on 5 October. Kenya has nine confirmed Ebola cases to date, with two deaths, all linked to the DRC outbreak that began 15 May across eight provinces and has tallied 11,042 cases and 5,387 deaths. Uganda’s outbreak, declared over on 26 August, involved 20 cases (15 imported from DRC) and two deaths. Related cases appeared in Nigeria and France; four evacuees went to the Netherlands, United Kingdom, and Germany. The Bundibugyo strain has no specific treatments; vaccines are in early human trials.

triage.headline_ja: ケニア、23日間新規感染なしで最後のエボラ患者を退院

triage.notes: 記事自体はケニアでの収束報告だが、根本原因であるDRCの大規模エボラ流行（2026年5月15日発生、11,042例・死亡5,387人）が継続中であり、対象国リストに含まれるためDRCのみverified_locationsに記載。ケニア・ウガンダ・ナイジェリア・欧州諸国は対象国リスト外のため除外。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola continuă să provoace victime în Congo, în timp ce Kenya anunță externarea ultimului pacient
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola continues to claim victims in Congo, as Kenya announces the discharge of the last patient.
article.articleSummary: Ebola continues to claim victims in the Democratic Republic of Congo, as Kenya discharges its last Ebola patient, initiating a 42-day period to be declared Ebola-free. Kenya reported nine infections since early October; the initial case, a Kenyan returning from the DRC, died after arrival. Of the eight remaining cases, one died and seven recovered; no new infections since 19 October. The last 11 contacts were released from quarantine on Wednesday, and Kenya will impose a 21-day quarantine on returnees from the DRC. In the DRC, 11,042 infections and 5,387 deaths have been reported, with about 2,990 recoveries; mortality 48.8%. The outbreak began in Ituri (north-east) and has spread to seven provinces, mainly Ituri and Nord-Kivu, marking the 17th Ebola outbreak there. No vaccine for Bundibugyo; MSF calls for Ervebo access; WHO started a cross-protection study in RDC on Oct 24. The epicenter Ituri faces armed conflict.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Monkeypox cases are rising in Brazil, and concerns are growing about travel between Brazil and Argentina.
article.articleSummary: As of 11 November 2026, monkeypox (mpox) cases are rising in Brazil, with São Paulo recording 64 cases in the month and Rio de Janeiro 74 in two months. Brazil Health Ministry reports 832 mpox cases nationwide, with increases in Ceará and Brasília. The trend raises cross-border concerns for Argentina due to travel linked to the São Paulo GP and a papal visit. Mpox spreads mainly through physical contact, especially skin lesions, and can spread via sexual contact, bodily fluids, and shared items. Symptoms include skin lesions, fever, muscle pains, headaches, and swollen lymph nodes. Argentina has 23 cases this year (one per week), including at least four of clade Ib detected in Córdoba, San Juan, and Buenos Aires Province; first seen in March in a Buenos Aires hospital. Brazil is negotiating 25,000 vaccine doses for high-risk groups; no mass vaccination due to transmission driven by physical contact.
