article.articleHeadline: Covid-19 em alta no Brasil: quem pode vacinar, sintomas e como se proteger
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: COVID-19 on the rise in Brazil: who can be vaccinated, symptoms and how to protect yourself.
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 is rising again in Brazil, with Fiocruz's InfoGripe signaling growth in Mato Grosso, Distrito Federal, São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, and Santa Catarina. While not a panic, experts urge vigilance, especially for the elderly, pregnant women, children, and the immunocompromised. Per the Ministério da Saúde, periodic vaccination is advised for adults 60+, pregnant women (one dose per pregnancy), children 6 months to under 5 years, and immunocompromised individuals; other priority groups include people with comorbidities, health workers, Indigenous, quilombolas, and ribeirinhos, with checks at a Unidade Básica de Saúde using the vaccination card. Symptoms include fever, chills, cough, fatigue, myalgia, headache, sore throat, nasal congestion, and runny nose; confirmation requires testing. Early identification guides treatment. Seek care for shortness of breath or worsening symptoms; older adults, immunocompromised and those with comorbidities should seek prompt medical evaluation. Brazil's SUS offers nirmatrelvir/ritonavir for eligible patients, started within five days of onset.

triage.headline_ja: ブラジルでCOVID-19が増加：接種対象者、症状、予防方法について
triage.triage_reason: COVID-19の季節的増加に関する通常の公衆衛生広報記事であり、異常性や国際的拡大リスクは認められず、既存の対策（ワクチン接種・治療薬提供）が機能している。
triage.notes: COVID-19は既知の疾患であり、ブラジル保健省・Fiocruzが通常の監視とワクチン接種・治療の啓発を行っている季節的増加の報道。新規性・異常性は認められない。

article.articleHeadline: Кому необходимо проверить антитела на корь
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Who needs to have their measles antibodies tested.
article.articleSummary: Russia advises measles antibody testing for adults who cannot recall when they were vaccinated; those aged about 35–40+ should check antibody levels and, if needed, receive revaccination. Epidemiologist and Russian Academy of Education vice-president Gennady Onishchenko says revaccination should occur every 10 years from the vaccination date, and adults should verify their vaccination status in medical records. He notes that before vaccination programs, measles exposure roughly matched birth rates, providing context. Separately, Rospotrebnadzor confirmed an imported Zika fever case in Moscow in a woman who recently returned from Bali; she was hospitalized in an infectious diseases hospital. A specialist interviewed by Vechernaya Moskva discussed Zika’s features and epidemic risk, highlighting monitoring rather than evidence of sustained local transmission.

triage.headline_ja: 麻疹抗体検査が必要なのは誰か
triage.triage_reason: ロシア国内向けの麻疹抗体検査啓発記事と、バリ島から帰国した女性のジカ熱輸入症例1件の報告であり、国内伝播や重大な公衆衛生上の影響を示す証拠はない。
triage.notes: 麻疹抗体検査の呼びかけは公衆衛生啓発であり感染症イベントのシグナルではない。ジカ熱症例はバリ島滞在中の感染によるモスクワでの輸入症例1件のみで、現地（インドネシア）での持続的伝播の証拠はないが、発生源地としてインドネシアを参考情報として記載。

article.articleHeadline: 50 años después de la identificación del ébola: el reto sanitario de hacer frente a todas sus variantes
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: 50 years after the identification of Ebola: the healthcare challenge of facing all its variants.
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo outbreak of 2026 tests Ebola response models that historically focused on a single species. Five decades after Ebola virus identification, four human-pathogenic species in the Orthoebolavirus genus—Zaire, Sudan, Bundibugyo, and Tai Forest—drive regional risk; Reston and Bombali have not caused human disease. The Zaire-centric approach has yielded vaccines, monoclonal antibody cocktails, and diagnostic assays, but these were developed against Zaire’s glycoprotein and validated on Zaire genomes, with cross-species protection assumed rather than measured. Bundibugyo’s sequence divergence shows that Zaire-based tests lose sensitivity, risking false negatives and undercounting non-Zaire infections. A comprehensive response requires pan-ebolavirus diagnostics plus species-specific tests, multivalent or mosaic vaccines and conserved T-cell epitope–based therapeutics, and rapid updates as antigenic data change. Continuous genomic surveillance and sustained operational readiness—beyond inventory—including simulation training and VR modules are essential to accelerate diagnosis, vaccine/therapy development, and outbreak response for future pathogens.

triage.headline_ja: エボラウイルス特定から50年：すべての変異種に対処する医療上の課題
triage.triage_reason: 2026年のブンディブギョ型エボラ流行が進行中であり、IHR基準の「異常・予想外」「国際的拡大リスク」に該当。複数の人獣共通感染症影響カテゴリを伴い、地域的脅威が確認されている。
triage.notes: 記事はコンゴ民主共和国のブンディブギョ型エボラ流行（2026年）を主題としており、IHRアナウシス基準の3つ以上に該当。発生地域にはウガンダ、スーダン、コートジボワールも列挙されているが、記事サマリー上で具体的な流行活動の記載はブンディブギョ（DRC内）に限定されているため、verified_locationsはDRCのみとした。複数のエボラウイルス種が地域的脅威として言及されており、診断・ワクチン・治療開発の課題が強調されている。

article.articleHeadline: Rośnie liczba zachorowań na ebolę. "Najbardziej śmiercionośna epidemia
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The number of Ebola cases is rising. "The most deadly epidemic."
article.articleSummary: Democratic Republic of the Congo reports the deadliest Ebola epidemic in its history. By 2026-11-11, there are more than 11,000 infections, with about half resulting in death (5,387 fatalities). The outbreak began in May, with Bundibugyo ebolavirus (BVD) spreading to eight of 26 provinces. CDC epidemiologists say sustained high transmission continues. WHO identifies fruit bats as the likely reservoir; initial spillover from wildlife (bats, primates) followed by human-to-human transmission via blood, secretions, and other bodily fluids. Transmission is especially intensified in health facilities with inadequate precautions and during burials with direct contact with the deceased. Incubation is 2–21 days. Early symptoms mimic other febrile illnesses: fever, fatigue, myalgia, headache, sore throat; lab testing is needed for confirmation. There are no vaccines yet; control focuses on rapid case identification, isolation, contact tracing, safe burials, and community education. In late October, WHO began testing two BVD vaccines; results expected early next year.

triage.headline_ja: エボラの感染者数が増加。「最も致死率の高い流行」
triage.triage_reason: DRCにおいて1万人超の感染、5,387人の死亡という過去最悪規模のエボラ流行であり、公衆衛生への深刻な影響、持続的なヒト-ヒト感染、ワクチン未確立など複数のIHR基準・WPRO基準に該当する。
triage.notes: 致死率約49%、8/26州に拡大、CDC・WHOが関与。ワクチン治験が進行中だが未承認。国際的な支援ニーズが高いと考えられる。

article.articleHeadline: Congo Ebola Outbreak Tops 11,000 Cases
article.articleSummary: Congo's Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak has surpassed 11,000 cases, with 5,387 deaths, and 11,042 infections reported by the health ministry, making it the deadliest outbreak in the country’s history. Declared in mid-May, it has spread to eight of Congo’s 26 provinces amid armed conflict, a strained health system, poor roads, and widespread mistrust that hinder containment. The Bundibugyo virus has no known vaccine or treatment, and health facilities have faced attacks and misinformation. The outbreak has crossed borders to Uganda, Kenya and Nigeria, though no totals for those countries are provided. No timeline for containment or vaccine is given; experts urge intensified efforts, noting the outbreak has, since declaration, produced about three times as many cases and deaths as the 2014–2016 West Africa outbreak did in a comparable period.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ出血熱流行、感染者数1万1000人を突破
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ(DRC)で過去最悪規模（感染1万1000人超、死亡5387人）のエボラ出血熱流行が発生し、複数国への越境拡大、ワクチン・治療法不在、武力紛争による対応困難という複合的な深刻事態であるため。
triage.notes: 記事はBundibugyo型エボラウイルスの流行について述べており、ワクチン・治療法が確立していない点、武装紛争・インフラ不備・不信感が封じ込めを妨げている点が特筆される。アンゴラ、ケニア、ウガンダ、ナイジェリアへの越境も報告されているが、具体的な症例数は記載されておらず、対象国リストにも含まれないため verified_locations から除外した。

locations.name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

article.articleHeadline: Surto de ébola na República Democrática do Congo ultrapassa 11 mil casos
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo surpasses 11,000 cases.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has surpassed 11,000 cases, with 11,042 infections and 5,387 deaths; 2,990 recoveries and 651 hospitalized or in isolation. Contact tracing is 79.7% complete. As of 9 November, Ituri (57.7%) and North Kivu (32.7%) account for the majority of new cases. The Bundibugyo strain, for which there is no vaccine or treatment, has spread to eight of 26 provinces. WHO is pursuing two vaccines; early human trials are safe, though development may take months. DRCongo began mass vaccination with Ervebo in late August, initially for the Zaire strain, with animal data suggesting protection against Bundibugyo. Ongoing violence in Ituri and North Kivu hampers response; health workers have been attacked. The outbreak spread to Uganda (20 cases, 15 imported, 2 deaths), Kenya (9 cases, 2 deaths), Nigeria (1 case), and France; four people were repatriated to the Netherlands, Germany, and the UK. This is the 17th Ebola outbreak in DRC and the second deadliest globally, behind the 2014–2016 West Africa outbreak. Transmission is via direct contact with bodily fluids; symptoms include severe fever, vomiting, diarrhea, and internal bleeding.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱アウトブレイク、1万1千例を突破
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ（ブンディブギョ株）アウトブレイクが1万人超・死亡5千人超に達し、複数国への国際的拡大、ワクチン未確立、紛争による対応阻害など深刻な公衆衛生事案であり、フルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 記事ではウガンダ・ケニア・ナイジェリア・フランス・オランダ・ドイツ・英国への拡大が報告されているが、対象国リストに該当するのはDRCのみ。ブンディブギョ株はワクチン未承認であり、既存エボラ対応（エルベボ）の有効性は動物データのみで確認中。紛争地域での対応困難が長期化要因。

locations.name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

article.articleHeadline: Kenia da de alta a su último paciente de ébola tras registrar 23 días sin nuevos contagios
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Kenya discharges its last Ebola patient after 23 days without new infections.
article.articleSummary: Kenya discharged its last Ebola patient after 23 days with no new infections, triggering a 42-day countdown to declare the outbreak over. Health Minister Aden Duale said there are no patients in treatment and no contacts in quarantine, with 11 contacts completing observation and returning home. The last confirmed Kenyan case was reported on October 19; the country has nine confirmed cases and two deaths, all linked to the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) outbreak declared May 15, which has affected eight DRC provinces and, per official tallies, 11,042 cases and 5,387 deaths. Uganda’s outbreak related to the same Congolese cluster ended August 26 (20 cases, 2 deaths; 15 imported). Nigeria and France have reported linked cases; four people were evacuated abroad (Netherlands, United Kingdom, Germany). The Bundibugyo strain has no specific treatment; vaccines are in early human trials and appear safe, but may take months to develop.

triage.headline_ja: ケニア、23日間新規感染なしでエボラ最後の患者を退院
triage.triage_reason: ケニアでの終息は朗報だが、背景にあるDRCのエボラ流行は11,042症例・5,387死亡という大規模かつ継続中の公衆衛生危機であり、複数国への越境拡大（ウガンダ、ナイジェリア、フランス、欧州への退避搬送）が確認されているため、フルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 記事自体はケニアでのエボラ終息を報じる内容だが、根本流行であるDRCのアウトブレイク（2026年5月15日宣言、8州に拡大、死亡率約49%）は対象国リストに該当し、国際的拡大（ウガンダ・ナイジェリア・フランスへの波及、オランダ・英国・ドイツへの患者退避）も確認されているため継続監視・評価が必要。ケニア・ウガンダ・ナイジェリア・フランス・オランダ・英国・ドイツは対象国リスト外のため除外。

article.articleHeadline: Epidemia di ebola in Congo, oltre 11.000 contagi e 5387 morti
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola epidemic in Congo, over 11,000 cases and 5,387 deaths.
article.articleSummary: As of 11 November 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo reports an Ebola outbreak with over 11,000 infections and 5,387 deaths, spanning eight of its 26 provinces. There is currently no vaccine or cure available. The World Health Organization warned last May about Bundibugyo ebolavirus, raising the epidemic risk from high to very high due to rapid spread. In a matter of months, confirmed cases surged from dozens to thousands, marking it as the deadliest outbreak the country has faced to date. The report underscores an urgent need for enhanced surveillance, supportive patient care, and robust containment efforts to curb transmission. Symptoms are not detailed in the report, but the mortality burden highlights the severity of this ongoing epidemic in the region.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでエボラ出血熱が流行、感染者1万1000人超、死者5387人
triage.triage_reason: DRCで過去最大規模のエボラ流行が発生し、致死率・感染拡大とも深刻でIHR基準を複数満たすため、フルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: WHOが5月にBundibugyoエボラウイルスの流行リスクを「高」から「非常に高い」へ引き上げたとの記述あり。ワクチン・治療法なしとされる点は要確認（既存のエボラワクチンとの整合性）。

article.articleHeadline: Najteža epidemija ebole u Kongu u povijesti: više od 11.000 zaraženih i 5387 umrlih
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The deadliest Ebola epidemic in Congo's history: more than 11,000 infected and 5,387 dead.
article.articleSummary: As of November 11, 2026, Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has 11,042 confirmed cases and 5,387 deaths, marking it the deadliest outbreak in the country’s history. The epidemic has accelerated quickly, with 1,000 confirmed cases reached in 40 days after response activation, far faster than the 2018 outbreak’s 235 days. Declared in May, it continues amid armed conflict, a strained health system, poor roads, and violence fueled by distrust and misinformation. The disease is caused by the Bundibugyo virus, for which no approved vaccine or specific treatment exists; two vaccine candidates are advancing—Oxford University with the Serum Institute of India, and Moderna. Trials will be led by the DRC’s National Institute for Biomedical Research with WHO support. Life-saving measures include early care, contact tracing, isolation, safe and dignified burials, and community engagement. The 2014–2016 West Africa outbreak reported about 28,000 cases and >11,000 deaths.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ史上最悪のエボラ出血熱流行：感染者11,000人以上、死者5,387人
triage.triage_reason: DRCにおけるエボラ出血熱が過去最悪の規模（感染者11,042人、死者5,387人）に達し、感染拡大速度も過去最速であるため、IHR基準・WPRO基準の双方で複数該当し社会的関心も高い。
triage.notes: 発生地域にAngolaが含まれているが、記事サマリーではDRC国内の流行のみが主題であり、Angolaへの拡大については言及がないため除外した。紛争地域での対応の困難さ、ワクチン未承認、ワクチン治験進行中などがリスク要因として挙げられている。

article.articleHeadline: O que é sarna humana, doença que causou suspensão de aulas em escolas de MG
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: What is human scabies, the disease that caused the suspension of classes in schools in Minas Gerais.
article.articleSummary: Two schools in Vespasiano, in the Belo Horizonte metropolitan area of Minas Gerais, suspended classes after scabies cases were identified, including a teacher at Escola Estadual Maria da Piedade Fonseca in Morro Alto; Escola Municipal de Ensino Especial Vovó Mariquita also halted activities, with classes expected to resume on Nov 12, 2026 after cleaning. Human scabies, caused by the Sarcoptes scabiei mite, causes intense nocturnal itching and skin lesions; transmission is mainly via prolonged skin-to-skin contact, with less frequent spread through shared clothing or bedding; it is not transmitted by cough. Treatment should be prescribed by health professionals and may include topical or oral medications; close contacts often require simultaneous treatment, and hygiene measures for linens and garments are important. The Minas Gerais SES reports 11 scabies outbreaks in 2026 across Campos Gerais, Paraguaçu, São Gonçalo do Pará, Belo Horizonte, Andradas, Lagoa Santa, Itapecerica, Lavras, Joaquim Felício, Coronel Xavier Chaves, and Alfenas.

triage.headline_ja: ヒト疥癬とは何か、ミナスジェライス州の学校で授業休止を引き起こした疾患
triage.triage_reason: 疥癬は公衆衛生上重篤度が低く、国際的拡大や渡航制限のリスクもないため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに該当せず見送りと判断する。
triage.notes: 疥癬は皮膚接触による感染で重症度・致死性は低く、ミナスジェライス州内の学校レベルの局所的な事例。州内で2026年に11件の集団発生が報告されているが、国際的な脅威やパンデミックポテンシャルはない。

article.articleHeadline: कांगो में सबसे बड़ा इबोला प्रकोप, संक्रमित हुए 11,042 में से आधे मरीजों की मौत, एक्सपर्ट ने चेताया
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Congo's largest Ebola outbreak; half of the 11,042 infected have died, an expert warned.
article.articleSummary: Congo's largest Ebola outbreak, caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, has reached 11,042 cases and 5,387 deaths in the Democratic Republic of Congo, with about half of those infected dead. The crisis spans eight of the 26 provinces, after being declared in May, and Ituri and North Kivu are the current hotspots amid renewed violence that hampers response. There is no vaccine or cure for this Bundibugyo strain. The outbreak has crossed borders to Uganda, Kenya, and Nigeria, signaling wider regional spread. Attacks on health workers and distrust of facilities further impede care delivery. Experts urge decisive action to stop transmission. The WHO/UN and national authorities consider this the second-largest Ebola outbreak since 1976, and UN World Food Programme acting executive director Karl Skau labels it the fastest-spreading Ebola outbreak to date.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ最大のエボラ流行、感染者11,042人のうち半数が死亡、専門家が警鐘
triage.triage_reason: 致死率約50%、死者5,387人、ワクチン・治療法のないBundibugyo株による史上第2位の大流行で、ウガンダ・ケニア・ナイジェリアへの越境拡大も報告されており、IHR基準の複数に該当する。
triage.notes: 記事はウガンダ、ケニア、ナイジェリアへの越境拡大を言及しているが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めない。主発生国はコンゴ民主共和国（DRC）。

article.articleHeadline: Чумата в Русия: В Иркутск с години пренебрегват опасността от зараза с патогени
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Plague in Russia: In Irkutsk, for years they have neglected the danger of infection with pathogens.
article.articleSummary: As of 11 November 2026, Irkutsk's anti-plague institute is under scrutiny after the death of 28-year-old Darya Shipilova, with officials saying no emergency situations involving pathogenic work were declared. The case centers on a suspected pneumonic plague linked to a broken tube containing plague pathogens; Shipilova was hospitalized on 29 September with pneumonia and died in the early hours of 2 October. About 200 contacts were isolated and several Irkutsk hospitals quarantined. Rospotrebnadzor states the death was due to pneumonia of unknown etiology, not confirmed plague. The investigation cites long-standing safety failures: 2015 warning for missing automatic fire alarms, 2019 biosafety-document omissions, June 2026 lack of decontamination plans and disinfectants, and September 2026 an outdated civil-defense plan. The institute, founded in 1934, has a Cold War-era legacy and participated in Russia–China infectious-disease exercises near the China border in Khabarovsk.

triage.headline_ja: ロシアのペスト：イルクーツクで何年も病原体感染の危険が放置されていた
triage.triage_reason: 疑わしい肺ペスト（未確認）による死亡例とバイオセーフティ施設の長年にわたる安全管理不備が判明し、公衆衛生上の深刻性と異常性が認められるためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 事案はロシア・イルクーツクの抗ペスト研究所で発生しており、対象国リストに該当する国はない。中国は国境付近での合同演習の文脈で言及されているのみで、発生地ではないため verified_locations から除外した。

article.articleHeadline: Cea mai gravă epidemie de Ebola din istoria statului Congo. Peste 5.300 de morți și 11.000 de infectări
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The most severe Ebola outbreak in the history of the Congo state. Over 5,300 deaths and 11,000 infections.
article.articleSummary: Democratic Republic of Congo is experiencing the most severe Ebola outbreak in its history, caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus. As of 11 November 2026, 11,042 laboratory-confirmed cases and 5,387 deaths have been reported, with half of diagnosed individuals dying. Declared in May, it is the 17th Ebola outbreak in the DRC and has surpassed all previous episodes in cases and fatalities. Transmission persists in eight of 26 provinces, with Ituri and North Kivu in the east most affected. Health teams face challenges identifying cases and tracing contacts amid damaged roads, long distances, and limited medical access; armed conflict and strikes impede responses; unpaid salaries disrupt several units; epidemiologic checkpoints suspended. Two experimental vaccines—Oxford University/Serum Institute of India and Moderna—are in WHO-coordinated INRB trials, but vaccines are not a substitute for case finding, care, isolation, and contact tracing. Cases linked to the outbreak have been reported in countries. EU risk remains low.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ史上最悪のエボラ流行、死者5,300人以上・感染者11,000人以上
triage.triage_reason: DRC史上最大規模のエボラ流行で致死率約50%、複数州にまたがる持続的伝播と紛争・医療アクセス制限による対応困難が確認されており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: 記事は『関連症例が複数国で報告』と述べるが具体国名は不明。EUリスクは低いとされている。ワクチン治験（Oxford/SII、Moderna）が進行中。

article.articleHeadline: Thông tin về hai trường hợp sốt xuất huyết Dengue có diễn biến rất phức tạp
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Information on two dengue fever cases with very complicated clinical courses.
article.articleSummary: Two dengue fever cases with very complicated clinical courses were reported on 11 November 2026 at the National Institute of Infectious and Tropical Diseases in Vietnam. Both patients were previously healthy. Case 1: B.H., 53, from Hai Phong, experienced about five days of high fever (39–40°C) with fatigue, nausea/vomiting and right upper-quadrant abdominal pain. Thrombocytopenia fell from 38 to 21 G/L; AST rose to 1,939 U/L and ALT to 804 U/L, with coagulopathy indicating severe dengue with acute liver injury and risk of circulatory compromise. Case 2: P.L., 23, from Hanoi, began around seven days of fever with chills, severe headache, myalgia and gastrointestinal symptoms. Platelets dropped to 21 G/L; AST 1,907 U/L and ALT 883 U/L; ultrasound revealed bilateral pleural effusions and intra-abdominal fluid, signaling plasma leakage and looming shock. Experts warn the dangerous phase often occurs when fever subsides (days 3–7); emphasize ICU monitoring, cautious paracetamol use, avoiding NSAIDs, rehydration, vector control, and vaccination guidance.

triage.headline_ja: 臨床経過が非常に複雑なデング熱症例2件に関する情報
triage.triage_reason: 個別の重症デング熱症例2件の報告であり、ベトナムで季節性に流行する疾患のため異常性は低いが、重症化・肝障害・血漿漏出などの重篤な経過がみられるため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 記事は個別の重症デング熱症例2例に関する臨床的警告であり、流行規模やクラスター発生の情報はない。デング熱はベトナムの風土病であり季節性流行の一部と考えられるが、重症度が高いため続報を注視する。

article.articleHeadline: Viruela del mono: aumentan los casos en Brasil y Argentina registra contagios de la variante más transmisible
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Monkeypox: Cases rise in Brazil, and Argentina reports infections of the most transmissible variant.
article.articleSummary: Monkeypox (mpox) cases rise in Brazil, totaling 832, according to the Health Ministry. São Paulo reports 64 new infections in the last month; Rio de Janeiro, 74 in the last two months, sevenfold higher than the same period in 2025, signaling regional transmission amid travel with Argentina. In Argentina, 2026 has 23 mpox cases, at least four of clade Ib, detected in Córdoba, San Juan, and Buenos Aires Province — a lineage with greater person-to-person transmission but lower fatality than West Africa’s ancestral strain. Brazil has purchased 25,000 additional vaccine doses, focused on high-risk groups rather than mass vaccination. Transmission is mainly through close contact with infected lesions; possible respiratory spread with prolonged exposure. Incubation 6–20 days; initial flu-like symptoms precede skin lesions. Antivirals exist; vaccination within four days of exposure can reduce severity; seek medical care after contact.

triage.headline_ja: サル痘：ブラジルで感染拡大、アルゼンチンでは最も感染力の強い変異株（クレードIb）の感染例を確認
triage.triage_reason: ブラジルでの症例急増とアルゼンチンでのクレードIb検出は国際的拡大・異常性の基準に該当し、IHR基準2つ以上を満たすためフルリスク評価に進むべきシグナルと判断。
triage.notes: アルゼンチンは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations から除外。ブラジルとアルゼンチン間の渡航による地域伝播の兆候が指摘されており、クレードIbの検出は国際的な公衆衛生上の懸念材料。致死率・重症度に関する具体的データは記事に記載なし。

article.articleHeadline: सेवाश्रम स्कूल में मलेरिया का कहर, 5वीं की छात्रा की इलाज के दौरान मौत, छोटा भाई अस्पताल में भर्ती
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Malaria wreaks havoc at Seva Shram School; a fifth-grade girl dies during treatment, younger brother admitted to hospital.
article.articleSummary: Malaria outbreak reported at Seva Shram School in Rayagada, Odisha, with the Badaraising Ashram School in Jemadeipenta Panchayat identified in reporting. A fifth-grade girl, Khushi Kilaka, died during malaria treatment after returning to the hostel from a 10-day break; fever developed soon after. Blood tests at Jemadeipenta Health Center confirmed malaria, and she was referred to the Rayagada District Headquarters Hospital where she died. Her younger brother also tested malaria-positive and is hospitalized under ongoing care. Health authorities have launched an investigation, screening other students, and implementing vector-control measures on campus, including cleaning and insecticide spraying, to prevent mosquito-borne diseases in ashram schools. Published 11 November 2026."} ,{

triage.headline_ja: セヴァシュラム学校でマラリア猛威、5年生の女子生徒が治療中に死亡、弟も入院
triage.triage_reason: 単一の寄宿学校内でのマラリア感染による死亡例であり、地元保健当局が既に媒介動物対策・スクリーニングを実施中。国際的拡大や渡航制限のリスクは低いが、学校内での感染継続の可能性があるため経過観察が必要。
triage.notes: インド・オディシャ州の寄宿学校（アシュラム・スクール）内でのマラリア集団発生。地元保健当局による調査・媒介動物対策が既に進行中であり、現時点では地域限定的な事案。続報で感染拡大の有無を確認する必要あり。

article.articleHeadline: WHO monitors PJ.2.1 COVID-19 variant as cases emerge globally
article.articleSummary: As of 11 November 2026, the WHO is monitoring PJ.2.1, a SARS-CoV-2 variant, as cases emerge across the United States, Singapore, Australia, New Zealand, Israel, France and Spain, with the variant first identified in Ontario, Canada in May. In the US, wastewater surveillance suggests PJ.2.1 may be the fastest-growing variant there. PJ.2.1 is a heavily mutated descendant of Omicron with spike-protein changes that could affect antibody binding. Current data show no evidence of greater severity than earlier variants, and most infections are expected to be mild; elderly and immunocompromised people remain at risk. India reports no confirmed widespread transmission and no restrictions. Symptoms resemble a cold or flu; diagnosis requires a COVID-19 test and variant confirmation needs genetic testing. Some early non-peer-reviewed studies propose tighter cell binding, but findings are inconclusive.

triage.headline_ja: WHOが世界各地で確認されているCOVID-19変異株PJ.2.1を監視
triage.triage_reason: WHOが新変異株PJ.2.1を監視しており国際的に複数国で感染が確認されているため、流行性・社会的関心の観点からフルRRAへの移行が妥当と判断した。
triage.notes: インドは発生地域リストに含まれるが、記事では『インドでは広範な感染拡大の確認はなく、制限措置もない』と明記されているため、対象国としては除外した。主な感染確認国（米国・シンガポール・豪州・NZ・イスラエル・仏・西・加）はいずれも対象国リストに該当しない。

article.articleHeadline: Kasus HIV di Kupang Capai 3.098, Yayasan Flobamora Jaya Peduli Minta Komitmen Pemda
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: HIV cases in Kupang reach 3,098; Flobamora Jaya Peduli Foundation calls for local government commitment.
article.articleSummary: HIV cases in Kupang City, Indonesia reach 3,098 as of September 2026, with 1,366 people living with HIV (PLWH) on antiretroviral therapy (ARV); 1,160 PLWH remain alive and supported by the Flobamora Jaya Peduli Foundation through September 2026. At a Kupang workshop on November 11, 2026, Mateus Da Silva, chair, urged local government commitment to sustain AIDS, TB, and Malaria (ATM) programs amid a transition away from global donor funding. Indonesia is committed to Ending AIDS by 2030 under the 95-95-95 targets: 95% of PLWH knowing their status, 95% of those on ARV, and 95% achieving viral suppression. The event stresses domestic funding and collaboration among government, legislators, civil society, and key populations to ensure continued program funding, protect vulnerable groups, and prevent new cases, deaths, or discrimination, thereby sustaining ATM outcomes in Kupang.

triage.headline_ja: クパンのHIV症例数が3,098人に到達、フロバモラ・ジャヤ・ペドゥリ財団が地方政府の取り組みを要請
triage.triage_reason: 慢性感染症であるHIVの累積症例報告と、資金継続に関する政策的呼びかけであり、急性の公衆衛生危機や異常事態ではないため。
triage.notes: 既知の慢性感染症（HIV/TB/マラリア）に関する資金・プログラム継続についての地域報道であり、新規アウトブレイクや急性公衆衛生イベントではない。ドナー資金撤退に伴う国内資金確保の政策的要請が主題。

article.articleHeadline: کورونا کی نئی قسم PJ.2.1 کی علامات عام نزلہ زکام اور فلو جیسی ہوسکتی ہیں، عالمی ادارۂ صحت کی وضاحت بخار، کھانسی، گلے میں درد اور تھکاوٹ کی صورت میں صرف علامات سے مرض کی شناخت ممکن نہیں؛ ماہرین نے ضرورت کے مطابق ٹیسٹ کرانے اور احتیاطی تدابیر اختیار کرنے کا مشورہ دیا ہے
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Symptoms of the new coronavirus variant PJ.2.1 may resemble the common cold and flu; WHO explains that fever, cough, sore throat and fatigue alone are not enough to diagnose the disease from symptoms; experts advise getting tested as needed and taking precautionary measures.
article.articleSummary: PJ.2.1, a new SARS-CoV-2 variant, may present with fever, cough, sore throat and fatigue similar to common cold or influenza; diagnosis cannot be made from symptoms alone. WHO notes testing is essential when treatment or public health actions depend on a precise diagnosis, as genomic sequencing is usually required to identify PJ.2.1, and standard COVID-19 tests do not specify the variant. First identified May 2026 in Ontario, Canada, with subsequent reports in the United States, Europe and the Asia-Pacific region. There is currently no evidence that PJ.2.1 causes more severe disease, higher hospitalization, or more deaths, though research is ongoing. High-risk groups include the elderly, immunocompromised, and patients with diabetes or chronic heart/lung diseases. Preventive steps: limit close contact, wear masks in crowded spaces, improve ventilation, and practice hand hygiene; seek urgent care if breathing difficulties or chest pain occur; rely on credible medical information as studies continue.

triage.headline_ja: 新型コロナウイルスの新変異株PJ.2.1の症状は一般的な風邪やインフルエンザに似ている可能性がある、WHOが説明：発熱、咳、喉の痛み、倦怠感だけでは病気を特定できない；専門家は必要に応じた検査と予防策の実施を推奨
triage.triage_reason: 新変異株PJ.2.1の出現が報告されているが、重症化や死亡率上昇のエビデンスは現時点でなく、対象国での具体的な発生確認も記事内で明示されていないため、続報を注視する段階と判断。
triage.notes: 記事はカナダ・オンタリオ州で初確認後、米国・ヨーロッパ・アジア太平洋地域で報告があったとする一般的な健康情報記事。発生地域リストに中国が含まれるが、記事サマリー内で中国における具体的な発生事例への言及はなく、対象国としての特定はできないため verified_locations は空とした。

article.articleHeadline: New Covid-19 variant PJ.2.1: Is it more contagious? Symptoms, vaccine, spread explained
article.articleSummary: PJ.2.1, a SARS-CoV-2 variant, was first documented in Ontario, Canada, in May 2026. Since then, cases have been identified in the United States, Spain, France, Israel, Singapore, Australia and New Zealand. Public Health Ontario genomic data show PJ.2.1 made up 25.2% of sequenced samples from Sept 20 to Oct 17, up from 16.9% earlier. Hong Kong reported the wider JN.1 lineage including PJ.2.1, but its PJ.2.1 share isn’t specified. Early lab work suggests the spike protein binds ACE2 more efficiently, potentially aiding spread, though there is no convincing evidence of greater severity, hospitalisations, or deaths. Symptoms resemble the common cold or flu, with severe sore throat and prolonged fatigue highlighted; others include fever, cough, runny nose, congestion, fatigue, headaches, muscle aches, and chills. Diagnosis requires testing and genomic sequencing. LP.8.1-adapted vaccines neutralise PJ.2.1 but are about 1.8-fold less sensitive to neutralising antibodies; real-world protection is uncertain. WHO monitors; vaccination is advised for vulnerable groups.

triage.headline_ja: 新型コロナウイルス新変異株PJ.2.1：感染力は強いのか？症状、ワクチン、拡大状況を解説
triage.triage_reason: 新変異株PJ.2.1が複数国に拡大しており、感染力増強の可能性があるためWPRO基準（異常性・持続曝露・流行しやすさ）に該当し、社会的関心（WHO監視等）もあることからフルRRAへ進める。
triage.notes: 疾患タグは『Influenza』だが記事内容はSARS-CoV-2新変異株PJ.2.1に関するもの。対象国リストのうち香港（中国）のみがJN.1系統（PJ.2.1含む）報告国として言及されているが、具体的な割合は不明。他の発生国（カナダ、米国、スペイン、フランス、イスラエル、シンガポール、豪州、NZ）は対象国リストに含まれないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola si v KDR vyžiadala už takmer 5400 obetí, boj s epidémiou komplikuje násilie
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola has claimed almost 5,400 lives in the DRC, and the fight against the outbreak is being complicated by violence.
article.articleSummary: By November 11, 2026, the Democratic Republic of Congo faces Ebola’s worst outbreak in its history, spanning eight provinces, with Ituri and North Kivu hardest hit. The death toll stands at about 5,400, while roughly 2,990 patients have recovered. It is the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record, after 2014–2016 West Africa. Violence hampers response, including an arson attack on a health center in Lolwa and disrupted interventions in Fataki. Disinformation and distrust hinder care seeking. For the Bundibugyo variant, there is no approved vaccine or specific treatment. WHO notes survivor ambulatory care is crucial; aid is being expanded and clinical vaccine trials are being prepared. The outbreak was officially declared in May 2026 and likely circulated weeks earlier.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱、死者数約5,400人に達する – 暴力が流行対策を複雑化
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国史上最大規模のエボラ流行（8州、死者約5,400人）であり、暴力による対応阻害やワクチン未承認など複数のIHR・WPRO基準に該当するため、フルリスク評価が必要と判断した。
triage.notes: 発生地域にAngolaが含まれているが、記事サマリーではDRC国内（Ituri、North Kivu等8州）のみが言及されており、Angolaへの拡大は言及されていないため除外した。国際的拡大リスクおよび渡航・貿易制限については記事中に明示的記載がなく不明とした。

article.articleHeadline: Kenya discharges last Ebola patient, beginning countdown to Ebola-free declaration
article.articleSummary: Kenya on Wednesday discharged its last Ebola patient, officially beginning a 42-day countdown toward an Ebola-free declaration. In October, Kenya recorded nine Ebola cases linked to a traveler who arrived from Congo through Uganda and transmitted the virus to four family members and four healthcare workers. The October cluster underscores ongoing transmission from imported cases and close contacts within the country's health system. The wider region has topped 11,000 Ebola cases since the outbreak began in May, highlighting regional spread despite Kenya's domestic milestone. Health authorities continue surveillance and contact tracing as the countdown proceeds, reflecting a focused effort to contain the outbreak while moving toward Ebola-free status.

triage.headline_ja: ケニア、最後のエボラ患者を退院させ、エボラ収束宣言へのカウントダウン開始
triage.triage_reason: DRCを起源とするエボラ流行が域内で1万1000人超の症例に達し、ウガンダ経由でケニアにも輸入・二次感染が発生するなど国際的拡大が確認されており、IHR基準に複数該当するためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はケニアでの輸入エボラ症例とその収束だが、ケニアとウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。流行の起源であり地域全体の感染源であるDRCのみを対象国として記載した。

article.articleHeadline: Cea mai gravă epidemie de Ebola din istoria statului Congo. Peste 5.300 de morți și 11.000 de infectări * Newsweek România
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The most severe Ebola outbreak in the history of the Congo. More than 5,300 deaths and 11,000 infections * Newsweek Romania
article.articleSummary: Democratic Republic of Congo faces the most deadly Ebola outbreak in its history, with more than 5,300 deaths and roughly 11,000 infections; official counts show 11,042 confirmed cases and 5,387 deaths. Declared in May, it is the 17th outbreak in the country, with transmission across eight of 26 provinces, most affected Ituri and North Kivu in the east. Response is hampered by violence and a weak health system, poor roads, and limited access; armed groups, unpaid salaries, and strikes disrupt operations. Checkpoints have suspended activity; misinformation fuels reluctance to test or seek care; attacks on health workers and resistance to safe burials are reported. The outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus; no approved vaccine or antiviral exists yet. Two experimental vaccines (Oxford/Serum Institute and Moderna) are in trials, coordinated by the DRC’s National Institute of Biomedical Research. WHO says vaccines complement, not replace, rapid diagnosis, care, isolation and contact tracing; EU risk remains very low. West Africa 2014–2016 had over 28,000 cases and ~11,000 deaths.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ史上最悪のエボラ出血熱流行。死者5,300人以上、感染者11,000人以上
triage.triage_reason: DRCで史上最大規模のエボラ流行（確認症例11,042、死亡5,387）が8州に拡大しており、公衆衛生への深刻な影響、治安悪化による対応困難、ワクチン未承認など複数のIHR・WPRO基準に該当するため。
triage.notes: 2026年5月に宣言された17次エボラ流行で、史上最悪規模。Bundibugyoエボラウイルスが原因で承認済みワクチン・抗ウイルス薬なし。治安悪化、誤情報、医療従事者への攻撃等が対応を阻害しており、国際的支援の必要性が高い。

article.articleHeadline: Covid-19: Goiás registra 25 mortes e mais de 200 casos graves da doença
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: COVID-19: Goiás records 25 deaths and more than 200 severe cases of the disease.
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 in Goiás, Brazil: the state recorded 25 deaths and 204 Covid-19–related severe acute respiratory syndrome (SRAG) cases this year, versus 710 SRAG cases and 127 deaths in 2025. Nationally, 17 states including Goiás and the Federal District reported a rise in mild cases in the six weeks to Oct 31. In Goiás, mild cases from August–October 2026 totaled 2,087, down from 10,389 in the same period of 2025 (−79.9%). The Secretaria de Saúde says Goiás’ Covid-19 activity remains within expected levels, with no sustained rise Aug–Oct 2026. Across Brazil, 118,851 Covid-19 cases have been notified this year (−68.8% vs 2025). Severe cases total about 3,400 (−63% from 9,200 last year) and deaths about 437 (−69% from 1,400). Prevention emphasizes vaccination (since 2024 for children 6 months–<5, pregnant people, and adults >60), hand hygiene, respiratory etiquette, physical distancing, and surface cleaning.

triage.headline_ja: COVID-19: ゴイアス州、25人の死亡と200件以上の重症例を記録
triage.triage_reason: COVID-19症例・死亡数は前年比で大幅減少しており、当局も「想定範囲内」と評価。異常性・拡大リスクともに低く、通常のサーベイランス報告に留まる。
triage.notes: 記事は前年比での症例・死亡数の減少傾向を報告する定期統計記事であり、新規の懸念事項や異常事態は確認されない。

article.articleHeadline: Novos casos de Covid-19 são registrados em 18 estados do Brasil; saiba como se proteger
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: New COVID-19 cases are reported in 18 states of Brazil; learn how to protect yourself.
article.articleSummary: Brazil reports rising COVID-19 activity across 18 states, with 118,851 influenza-like illness (ILI) notifications associated with SARS-CoV-2 through Nov 4, 2026. Severe acute respiratory syndrome (SRAG) linked to coronavirus is increasing in Mato Grosso, São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, Santa Catarina, and the Federal District, while mild infections rise in Alagoas, Bahia, Ceará, Espírito Santo, Goiás, Paraíba, Pernambuco, Piauí, Paraná, Roraima, and Rio Grande do Sul. In the same period last year there were 367,640 cases, about 67.7% more, indicating a year-over-year difference. In epidemiological week 41 (through Oct 17), SARS-CoV-2 accounted for roughly 50% of positives on panels testing for SARS-CoV-2, influenza A and B, and RSV. Vaccination remains central: routine doses for children 6 months to <5 years, pregnant people, and those ≥60; boosters for other adults depend on immunization history. Masking and ventilation advised, especially for symptomatic or vulnerable individuals.

triage.headline_ja: ブラジル18州で新たなCOVID-19感染例が報告、予防法を知ろう
triage.triage_reason: COVID-19の季節的な増加であり、前年比では減少傾向。重症例増加地域もあるが、既知の病原体かつ対策（ワクチン・マスク）が確立されており、国際的拡大や渡航制限のリスクは低い。
triage.notes: 既知の季節性COVID-19流行であり、前年同期比で67.7%減少。SRAGの増加地域（マトグロッソ、サンパウロ等）は一部あるが、全体として管理可能な状況と見られる。続報での重症度・死亡率の推移を注視。

article.articleHeadline: Opinião - A Covid ainda está entre nós, sem ser mortal, mas preocupa sim: em Porto Velho tem perto de 50 novos casos
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Opinion - COVID-19 is still among us, not deadly, but it is indeed concerning: in Porto Velho there are around 50 new cases.
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 remains among us in Porto Velho, Brazil, with around 50 new cases reported this year. All cases have been mild, with no hospitalizations or deaths. Brazil has seen about 716,000 COVID-19 deaths, with Rondônia state totaling 7,172 and Porto Velho accounting for 1,708. Last year, Brazil recorded 18 deaths, two of them in Porto Velho. Semusa, the Porto Velho health secretariat, urges keeping vaccination up to date per Ministry of Health guidelines and visiting a Basic Health Unit (UBS) to verify vaccination status and receive recommended doses. Seek urgent care if shortness of breath or significant symptoms develop. The virus has lost much of its lethality but remains circulating, requiring continued vigilance and vaccination.

triage.headline_ja: オピニオン - コロナウイルスは依然として私たちの中にある、致死的ではないが確かに懸念される：ポルトベーリョでは新規感染者が約50人
triage.triage_reason: 軽症例のみで入院・死亡もなく、既知のCOVID-19の流行であり異常性や国際的拡大リスクは認められない。
triage.notes: オピニオン記事であり、地域の保健当局がワクチン接種の継続を呼びかける内容。新規事例は全て軽症で特段のシグナルには該当しない。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola: Letzter Ebola-Patient in Kenia aus Klinik entlassen
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola: Last Ebola Patient in Kenya Discharged from Hospital.
article.articleSummary: Kenya has discharged the last Ebola patient, with seven survivors among nine total cases and no infections among the nine contacts, according to Health Minister Aden Duale. To be declared Ebola-free, Kenya must wait 42 days (two incubation cycles) without a new case, which would be December 23. Kenya’s first Ebola case emerged on October 6; the patient contracted in the Democratic Republic of Congo traveled by land through Uganda to Kenya, where he died in hospital. A family member who developed symptoms and was quarantined also died in mid-October. In the Democratic Republic of Congo, the outbreak remains uncontrolled across eight provinces, with more than 11,000 cases and about 5,400 deaths. The milestone is significant for Kenya’s tourism-driven economy ahead of peak travel season.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱：ケニアで最後のエボラ患者が退院
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国（DRC）では8州にまたがり11,000人超の感染・約5,400人の死亡という制御不能な大規模エボラ流行が続いており、既に国境を越えてウガンダ・ケニアへ感染が拡大した実績があるため、IHR基準を複数満たしシグナルとして採用する。
triage.notes: 記事はケニアでの輸入症例終息を報じているが、感染源であるDRCでは流行が制御不能な状態で継続しており、DRCを主たる発生国として評価した。ケニア・ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations から除外。

article.articleHeadline: Kongo'da Ebola salgınında vaka sayısı 11 bini aştı
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: In Congo, the Ebola outbreak case count has surpassed 11,000.
article.articleSummary: As of 11 November 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo reports 11,042 Ebola cases and 5,387 deaths, with roughly half of those infected succumbing. The outbreak, linked to Bundibugyo Ebola virus, was declared in mid-May and is the deadliest Ebola event in Congo’s history, with the virus spreading to 8 of the 26 provinces, notably Ituri and North Kivu. There is no approved vaccine or treatment for Bundibugyo. Ongoing conflict, health system crises, limited access, and widespread distrust hinder containment efforts, including repeated attacks on health workers and facilities. Authorities urge cessation of clashes to allow safe patient access. Experts warn that stronger, broader measures are needed, and note spillovers into neighboring countries, including Uganda, Kenya, and Nigeria. By comparison, the 2014-2016 West Africa outbreak infected ~28,000 people and caused >11,000 deaths.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでのエボラ出血熱流行、症例数が1万1千人を超える
triage.triage_reason: DRCにおけるエボラ出血熱流行は史上最悪規模（11,042例、5,387死亡）であり、近隣国への拡散や治療法未承認など深刻性・異常性・国際的拡大リスクが高いため、フルRRAへの移行が必要。
triage.notes: 記事はコンゴ民主共和国（DRC）における流行を主題としており、ウガンダ・ケニア・ナイジェリアへのスピルオーバーが言及されているが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations から除外。Ituri州はDRC国内の行政区分であり別個の国としては扱わない。

article.articleHeadline: Advogado e jornalista Sidnei Carvalho morreu durante viagem de trabalho após complicações de dengue
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Lawyer and journalist Sidnei Carvalho died during a business trip after dengue complications.
article.articleSummary: Sidnei Carvalho Pimentel, 59, a Brazilian lawyer specializing in tax law and a former journalist, died on 10 November 2026 in São Paulo from complications of dengue fever. Diagnosed before traveling for professional commitments with his wife Nubya Cirqueira, his condition worsened upon arrival, necessitating ICU admission, intubation, and hemodialysis, but he did not survive. He was co-owner of Pimentel, Kirian & Castro Advogados and counted Miguel Cançado, former president of OAB-GO, among close professional partners. The Goiás OAB lamented his loss, praising his technical excellence in tax law. Sidnei studied Journalism at the Federal University of Goiás (1989) and Law at PUCG Goiás, and left behind his wife and two children, Lara (law student) and Vinícius (journalist). Colleagues recall him as generous, attentive, and deeply engaged in Goiânia’s legal and media circles.

triage.headline_ja: 弁護士でジャーナリストのシドネイ・カルヴァリョ氏、デング熱の合併症で出張中に死去
triage.triage_reason: 個人の訃報記事であり、ブラジルにおけるデング熱の集団発生や公衆衛生上の異常事態を示す情報は含まれていない。
triage.notes: ブラジルはデング熱が地域流行している国だが、本記事は特定個人の死亡事例の訃報であり、アウトブレイクや公衆衛生上の新たな事象を報じるものではないため、対象国としての特記事項なし。

article.articleHeadline: Aulas são suspensas em escola na Grande BH por professora com sarna humana
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Classes are suspended at a school in Greater Belo Horizonte due to a teacher with scabies.
article.articleSummary: Scabies linked to a teacher at Escola Estadual Maria da Piedade Fonseca in Morro Alto, Vespasiano, near Belo Horizonte, prompted class suspension on 11 November 2026. The Minas Gerais Health Secretariat confirmed the case, the second in the municipality after another school reported scabies in a short interval. The school notified health authorities; contacts of the teacher were advised to seek medical evaluation. Pest control (dedetização) is planned for 11–12 November, with classes resuming after cleaning and health follow-up to minimize disruption to the academic calendar. A separate school in Vespasiano, Escola Municipal de Ensino Especial Vovó Mariquita, was also closed temporarily. The state reports 11 scabies outbreaks in 2026 across Minas Gerais, including Belo Horizonte and municipalities such as Campos Gerais, Paraguaçu, São Gonçalo do Pará, Andradas, Lagoa Santa, Itapecerica, Lavras, Alfenas. Transmission is by direct, prolonged skin contact; symptoms include intense itching and nocturnal skin lesions.

triage.headline_ja: ベロオリゾンテ近郊の学校で、疥癬に罹患した教師により授業が休止
triage.triage_reason: 疥癬は一般的に重症度・国際的拡大リスクが低い皮膚感染症であり、学校単位の局所的対応で管理可能なため、IHR・WPRO基準のいずれにも該当しない。
triage.notes: 疥癬は直接・長期の皮膚接触で感染し、ミナスジェライス州内で複数の小規模なアウトブレイクが報告されているが、重症度・国際的影響は低く地域の保健当局により管理可能と判断される。

article.articleHeadline: Pernambuco registra tendência de alta nos casos graves de metapneumovírus, aponta Fiocruz
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Pernambuco records an upward trend in severe human metapneumovirus cases, Fiocruz says.
article.articleSummary: Fiocruz’s Infogripe bulletin notes an upward trend in Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SRAG) caused by metapneumovirus in Pernambuco and other Northeast states, mainly affecting children and the elderly. Pernambuco’s SES-PE says local SRAG notifications declined recently and do not yet indicate a metapneumoviral surge. In 2026 Pernambuco reported 6,228 SRAG cases and 116 deaths (1.2 per 100,000). Among fatalities, 44% were over 60 and 54% male; 2,891 cases were in infants under one year. Most cases involve rhinovirus and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) among children, with SRAG not specified and influenza and COVID-19 accounting for smaller shares. The Recife Metropolitan Region had 3,826 cases, followed by Mata Sul and Sertão do São Francisco. Officials urge vaccination to prevent severe disease, noting coverage remains below targets, including for COVID-19, with vaccines available at public health posts.

triage.headline_ja: ペルナンブーコ州、重症メタニューモウイルス症例が増加傾向、フィオクルスが指摘
triage.triage_reason: ブラジル北東部でメタニューモウイルスによる重症呼吸器症候群（SRAG）の増加傾向が指摘されているが、地元保健当局はまだ急増を確認しておらず、情報が限定的であるため経過観察が妥当。
triage.notes: 地方保健当局（SES-PE）は、州レベルでは明確な急増を確認していないとしており、フィオクルスの全国的傾向分析との間に見解の差がある。小児・高齢者への影響が主で、ワクチン接種率の低さが懸念材料として挙げられている。

article.articleHeadline: Kongo'da Ebola salgınında can kaybı 5 bini aştı
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The death toll from the Ebola outbreak in Congo has surpassed 5,000.
article.articleSummary: Democratic Republic of Congo’s Ebola outbreak, which began on May 5, has killed 5,387 people and infected 11,042, according to government updates. Eight of the country’s 26 provinces have been affected, indicating broad geographic spread as the outbreak persists. The Bundibugyo Ebola strain is involved, and there are no approved treatments or vaccines for this strain. The outbreak is described as the second-largest and among the deadliest Ebola epidemics on record, following the 2014–2016 West Africa outbreak that caused more than 11,000 deaths. The article notes a continuing rise in fatalities and cases and highlights ongoing transmission within the Democratic Republic of Congo, with concerns about further spread across Africa.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでのエボラ出血熱流行、死者数5000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: DRCにおけるエボラ(ブンディブギョ株)の大規模流行で、死者5,387人・感染者11,042人、26州中8州に拡大しており、承認された治療薬・ワクチンもないため公衆衛生上深刻かつ国際的拡大リスクが高い。
triage.notes: Angolaは発生地域に含まれるが対象国リストに無く、またサマリー本文でも言及なし。承認治療薬・ワクチンがない株であり、史上2番目の規模とされる重大流行。

article.articleHeadline: Ébola: Quénia dá alta ao último doente, após 23 dias sem novos casos
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola: Kenya discharges the last patient after 23 days without new cases.
article.articleSummary: Kenya discharged the last Ebola patient after 23 days without new cases, launching a 42-day countdown to be declared Ebola-free. Health Minister Aden Duale said 11 of 135 contacts in quarantine had returned home after completing the observation period without symptoms; for the first time since the outbreak began there are no patients in treatment and no contacts in quarantine. The last confirmed Kenyan case was reported on October 19, with no community transmission. Kenya has nine confirmed cases and two deaths linked to the Congo DR Ebola outbreak that began in May, affecting eight Congolese provinces. The outbreak also reached Uganda (the WHO later declared the Ugandan outbreak finished) and was detected in Nigeria and France; four people were transferred from DRC to the Netherlands, the United Kingdom and Germany. The Bundibugyo strain has no specific treatment; WHO is testing two vaccines in humans, development may take months.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ:ケニア、23日間新規症例なしで最後の患者を退院
triage.triage_reason: DRC由来のエボラアウトブレイクは既にケニア・ウガンダ・ナイジェリア・欧州複数国へ拡大した実績があり、IHR基準（深刻な公衆衛生影響・国際的拡大リスク）に2つ該当するため。
triage.notes: 記事はケニアでの終息進展を報じるフォローアップ記事だが、ケニアは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。発端であるDRCのアウトブレイクは継続中であり、国際的拡大（ウガンダ、ナイジェリア、仏独蘭）の実績があるためリスクは依然高い。ワクチン治験中、ブンディブギョ株には特異的治療法なし。

article.articleHeadline: Ebolos protrūkis KDR: užsikrėtusiųjų skaičius viršijo 11 tūkst.
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in the DRC: the number of people infected surpassed 11,000.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 11,000 confirmed cases, with 11,042 infections and 5,387 deaths; about 2,990 recoveries. The outbreak is the largest in the country's history, caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, spreading via contact with body fluids and causing severe hemorrhagic fever. Originating in northeastern Ituri province, it has spread to seven other provinces, with most cases in Ituri and North Kivu; infections have also been reported in Uganda, Kenya, and Nigeria. No vaccines or treatments exist specifically for Bundibugyo; the WHO announced that Ervebo (Zaire strain) will be tested in a clinical trial in DRC to assess partial protection against Bundibugyo. Security challenges in eastern DRC—Ituri instability, health facility attacks (Lolvo village), suspension in Fataki area—complicate control, while ADF-linked attacks have occurred in Ituri, South Kivu, and North Kivu.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱アウトブレイク：感染者数が11,000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: DRCで史上最大規模のエボラ（ブンディブギョ株）アウトブレイクが発生し、11,000人超の感染、5,000人超の死亡、ウガンダ・ケニア・ナイジェリアへの国際的拡大が報告されているためフルRRAへ進める。
triage.notes: ウガンダ・ケニア・ナイジェリアでも感染例が報告されているが、いずれも対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations から除外。治安悪化（ADF関連攻撃、医療施設への攻撃）が対応を複雑化させている点も注視すべき。

article.articleHeadline: Die Vogelgrippe H5N1 zirkuliert weltweit ungehemmt: Wie gross ist die Gefahr für Menschen?
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The H5N1 avian influenza is circulating worldwide unabated: How great is the danger to humans?
article.articleSummary: H5N1 avian influenza is circulating worldwide, devastating wild birds and spreading to mammals. In the United States, dairy-cattle outbreaks since 2023 have led to human infections; in Washington state, on 1 November 2026 a death occurred, the third case in four weeks. Since 2024 the US has recorded three human deaths and 74 infections, with over 40 linked to cows and more than 20 to poultry; several sources remain unclear. No sustained human-to-human transmission has been observed. A Nature study reports the cattle-circulating H5N1 has mutated to bind mammalian cells, a first step toward infection. Globally, risk remains low, yet the animal reservoir allows further adaptation. Other avian subtypes circulating include H5N2, H9N2, H3N8, H10N5; H7N9 in China has more than 1,500 infections and over 600 deaths. Vaccines exist for H5.

triage.headline_ja: H5N1鳥インフルエンザが世界中で制御不能に拡大：人間への危険度はどれほどか？
triage.triage_reason: 米国での乳牛由来H5N1感染による死亡例の継続的発生と、哺乳類細胞への結合変異が報告されており、IHR基準の複数（深刻性・異常性・国際拡大リスク）に該当するためフルリスク評価に進むべきと判断。
triage.notes: 記事は主に米国での乳牛由来H5N1感染拡大とワシントン州での死亡例を扱っており、対象国リストに含まれる国（中国など）は過去の累計統計（H7N9の歴史的データ）として言及されているのみで、現行の発生事象の主題ではないため verified_locations には含めなかった。

article.articleHeadline: டெங்கு, மலேரியா முதல் ஆபத்தான விப்ரியோ பாக்டீரியா வரை: இந்தியாவில் அதிகரிக்கும் தொற்றுநோய் ஆபத்துகள்!
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: From Dengue and Malaria to Dangerous Vibrio Bacteria: Increasing Infectious Disease Risks in India!
article.articleSummary: India faces mounting infectious disease risks driven by extreme heatwaves, disease spread and air pollution, per the 2026 Lancet Countdown reports. In India, heatwave days from 2016 to 2025 were about half attributable to climate change, with roughly 193 billion potential work hours lost annually. The 2026 Lancet Countdown on Health and Climate Change warns that changing climate conditions are impairing sleep, productivity and livelihoods, and urges recognizing climate change as a global health emergency. The reports note that evolving environmental conditions have increased risks of dengue and malaria, and waterborne diseases, while air pollution continues to cause substantial premature deaths. Vulnerable pathogens such as dangerous Vibrio bacteria are highlighted as infection risks, underscoring rising disease threats in India as the climate crisis escalates.

triage.headline_ja: デング熱、マラリアから危険なビブリオ菌まで：インドで増加する感染症リスク！
triage.triage_reason: 特定の発生イベントではなく、気候変動と感染症リスクに関する一般的な報告（Lancet Countdown）の紹介記事であり、具体的な症例数・アウトブレイクの報告がないため見送り。
triage.notes: 本記事は特定の感染症アウトブレイクの報告ではなく、気候変動による将来的な感染症リスク増加に関する総説記事。具体的な患者数・発生地域の詳細がなく、続報や関連する具体的アウトブレイク報告があれば再評価が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola si v KDR vyžiadala už takmer 5400 obetí, boj s epidémiou komplikuje násilie
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola has already claimed nearly 5,400 lives in the DRC, the fight against the epidemic is complicated by violence.
article.articleSummary: The Democratic Republic of Congo is experiencing the worst Ebola outbreak in its history, spanning eight provinces with Ituri and North Kivu hardest hit. Violence against health workers and public distrust are undermining response efforts. Official data from the National Institute for Public Health report 11,042 confirmed Ebola cases and 5,387 deaths, with about 2,990 recoveries. The outbreak was officially declared in May, though experts believe the virus circulated weeks earlier. The crisis remains ongoing, complicated by security threats that hamper containment, case finding, and care delivery across affected regions.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ出血熱による死者が約5400人に、暴力が流行対策を複雑化
triage.triage_reason: DRC史上最悪規模のエボラ流行で、8州に拡大し死者数が多数、医療従事者への暴力が対応を阻害しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するため。
triage.notes: 史上最悪規模のエボラ流行で、11,042症例・5,387死亡と報告されており、暴力・住民の不信感が対応を妨げている。国際的な支援ニーズが高いと考えられる。

article.articleHeadline: Oltre 11mila casi di Ebola censiti in Repubblica Democratica del Congo - Sanità
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Over 11,000 Ebola cases recorded in the Democratic Republic of the Congo - Health
article.articleSummary: As of 11 November 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo has reported 11,042 Ebola infections and 5,387 deaths among 2,990 recoveries, yielding a 48.8% mortality rate. The outbreak began in Ituri province, with the majority in Ituri and North Kivu, and has spread to other provinces. The virus has crossed borders, with cases in Uganda, Kenya, and Nigeria. Over the past 50 years, Ebola has caused more than 15,000 deaths in Africa; in 2018–2020, 2,300 deaths occurred among 3,500 cases. The current epidemic was officially declared by Congolese authorities only after several months’ delay. Data cited are from the Institut national de santé publique (InSP).

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国で11,000人超のエボラ症例を記録 - 保健
triage.triage_reason: 致死率48.8%の大規模エボラ流行が複数州に拡大し、ウガンダ・ケニア・ナイジェリアへの越境伝播も報告されており、IHR基準に複数該当する深刻な公衆衛生イベントである。
triage.notes: ウガンダ・ケニア・ナイジェリアへの越境症例が報告されているが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsには含めていない。発生の中心はDRC（イトゥリ州・北キブ州）。宣言の遅れも指摘されており、対応能力への懸念材料となる。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola: UAE Lifts Visa Ban on Ugandans, Retains Restrictions on DR Congo, South Sudan
article.articleSummary: UAE lifts visa suspension for Ugandan nationals, allowing entry for Ugandan passport holders who have spent at least 21 days outside Uganda; DR Congo and South Sudan nationals remain restricted due to ongoing Ebola activity. Transit through the UAE remains restricted unless travelers have spent more than 21 days outside the three countries. Ugandan students in the UAE before June 2026, their families, embassy staff, and Ugandan diplomatic/special passport holders are exempt under approved procedures; humanitarian and medical exemptions are considered case-by-case. In Nigeria, the NCDC reports no new Ebola case since an imported Bundibugyo virus disease case from Uganda on Oct 20, 2026; 28 exposed contacts remain under monitoring as of Nov 9, with 62 total identified and 34 completing a 21-day follow-up. Ongoing surveillance, contact tracing, and lab testing continue; dengue in Sokoto/Zamfara and chikungunya in Sokoto; diphtheria and meningitis vigilance urged. Toll-free line 6232 for guidance.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱：UAEがウガンダ人へのビザ停止を解除、DRコンゴ・南スーダンへの制限は継続
triage.triage_reason: ウガンダ由来のエボラ（ブンディブギョウイルス）症例がナイジェリアに輸入され、UAEが複数国に対する渡航制限を継続・調整していることから、国際的拡大リスクと渡航制限の両方が確認され、IHR基準の複数項目に該当する。
triage.notes: 記事はウガンダ・南スーダン・DRコンゴでのエボラ（ブンディブギョウイルス）活動に関連するUAEの渡航制限とナイジェリアでの輸入症例・接触者監視を中心に報じている。対象国リストのうちDRコンゴのみが該当し、ウガンダ・南スーダン・ナイジェリア・UAEは対象国リスト外のため除外した。デング熱・チクングニア熱等ナイジェリア国内の併発情報は主題のエボラ関連情報に付随するもの。

article.articleHeadline: El Niño will cause 'pandemic-scale mortality'
article.articleSummary: El Niño 2026-27, predicted to be the most intense on record, could cause pandemic-scale mortality worldwide and should be classified as a public health emergency of international concern. Early analyses project up to 451,000 heat-related excess deaths between June 2026 and February 2027, with nearly half a million deaths when heat coincides with outbreaks of dengue fever, cholera, and other infectious diseases. Nigeria is expected to bear the largest heat-related toll (about 31,400 deaths between September 2026 and February 2027), followed by Indonesia and Sudan. The projections come from the Climate Impact Lab (University of Chicago) in a study not yet peer-reviewed. El Niño, a naturally occurring climate phenomenon intensified by warming oceans, can trigger heat, storms, droughts and wildfires, threatening crops and health. WMO COP31 updates and UN climate officials frame the crisis as a global health emergency of pandemic proportions.

triage.headline_ja: エルニーニョが「パンデミック規模の死亡」を引き起こす可能性
triage.triage_reason: 本記事は実際の感染症アウトブレイク報告ではなく、気候変動（エルニーニョ）に関する未査読の将来予測研究の紹介であり、具体的な発生事例情報がないため見送りとする。
triage.notes: 記事は査読前の気候影響予測研究（Climate Impact Lab, University of Chicago）に基づくもので、特定の感染症アウトブレイクの実発生を報告していない。ナイジェリア・インドネシア・スーダンは将来の熱関連死亡予測における例示国であり、対象国リストのIndonesiaも主題としての発生国ではないため verified_locations には含めない。

article.articleHeadline: 2 Anakan Sapi di Jembrana Mati akibat Rabies, Tertular Gigitan Anjing Liar
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Two Calves in Jembrana Regency Die of Rabies, Contracted from a Bite by a Wild Dog.
article.articleSummary: Rabies outbreak in Bali: Two calves in Pangyangan Village, Pekutatan District, Jembrana Regency, Bali, Indonesia, died after rabies infection, with transmission suspected from bites by wild dogs around the farm. Reports were received on October 27 and 31, 2026, and veterinary teams confirmed the diagnosis via laboratory testing. One calf displayed classic rabies symptoms—excessive drooling and aggressive behavior—and ran into a river near the site before dying. Laboratory results confirmed rabies positivity. Calves are more vulnerable due to frequent interaction with roaming dogs, which can bite multiple animals per transmission cycle. Preventive measures include vaccinating dogs in and around the outbreak area, with about 98% vaccination coverage reported; vaccination of unvaccinated dogs found during area surveys continues. Community information and education campaigns accompany these measures. The next step is stray-dog population control, implemented upon official village requests through the Jembrana Rabies Task Force.

triage.headline_ja: ジェンバラナ県の子牛2頭、野犬に噛まれて狂犬病感染し死亡
triage.triage_reason: 動物（子牛）の狂犬病感染事例であり、ヒトへの感染や公衆衛生上の深刻な影響は報告されておらず、既にワクチン接種98%と対策も進行中であるため見送り。
triage.notes: 動物（家畜）の狂犬病事例であり、ヒト感染や公衆衛生上の重大な懸念は記載なし。地域の狂犬病対策タスクフォースが対応中。

article.articleHeadline: تأكيد حالة وفاة مؤكدة بالحمى الصفراء في مقاطعة موروبو - Radio Tamazuj
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Confirmed death due to yellow fever in Morobo County - Radio Tamazuj.
article.articleSummary: Yellow fever fatalities confirmed in Morobo County, Central Equatoria, South Sudan. A 48-year-old farmer who recently traveled to the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) developed fever, headache, fatigue, chest and joint pain on Oct 24, followed by nosebleed and a rash; he was admitted to an isolation unit on Oct 29 and died on Nov 1. Initial Ebola tests were negative; RT-PCR confirmed yellow fever. South Sudan's Ministry of Health activated an emergency response with WHO, Africa CDC, and partners. A multi-disciplinary field team was dispatched to Morobo to conduct active case finding and contact tracing in Okaba village, Golombi. Investigations include reviewing health facility records, collecting blood and mosquito samples, and assessing potential local transmission. Cross-border surveillance with DRC authorities will guide vaccination campaigns and monitoring. Public urged to use nets, remove mosquito breeding sites, seek care for fever, jaundice, dark urine, or unusual bleeding. Hotline 6666.

triage.headline_ja: モロボ郡で黄熱病による死亡例を確認 - Radio Tamazuj
triage.triage_reason: 南スーダン中央エクアトリア州モロボ郡で黄熱病による死亡例が確認され、当初エボラ出血熱が疑われた。DRCへの渡航歴があり国境を越えた監視が行われているが、確定症例は対象国（DRC等）内では報告されていないため、今後の越境拡大の有無を注視する必要がある。
triage.notes: 確定症例は南スーダン（対象国外）で発生。DRCへの渡航歴がある患者であり、DRC当局との越境サーベイランスが実施されているが、DRC国内での確定症例報告はないため、対象国としては含めず。今後DRC側での症例報告があれば再評価が必要。

article.articleHeadline: La lucha contra el ébola en África: los desafíos sanitarios para contener la epidemia
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Fight Against Ebola in Africa: The Health Challenges to Contain the Epidemic.
article.articleSummary: Ebola (Bundibugyo virus) remains active in Africa, concentrated in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) with ongoing international surveillance by WHO and ECDC. The outbreak, declared May 15, 2026, shows thousands of confirmed cases and deaths across eight provinces: Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Tshopo, Haut/Uele, Bas/Uele, Ubangi Nord and Ubangi Sud. As of Nov 9, INSP data report 11,042 confirmed cases and 5,387 deaths (case fatality rate 48.8%), with Ituri leading at 7,684 cases and 3,628 deaths and North Kivu at 2,737/1,505; North Kivu’s CFR 55%, Ituri 47.2%. In the latest day, 52 new cases (Ituri 30, North Kivu 17, Alto Uele 5) were recorded. ECDC counts 10,990 cases and 5,354 deaths (as of Nov 8). Contact tracing covers 33,900 contacts in six provinces; 27,012 were supervised (~79.7%), below the 95% target. Community deaths (335 of 512) outpaced treatment centers (177). Security and resource constraints hinder response; IPC scores are below target (e.g., Kivu Norte 44.7%).

triage.headline_ja: アフリカにおけるエボラとの闘い：流行封じ込めに向けた保健上の課題
triage.triage_reason: DRCでエボラ（ブンディブギョウイルス）の大規模流行が継続中で、致死率約48.8%、1万人超の感染者・5千人超の死亡者を記録し、接触者追跡や感染制御が目標未達であるため、フルRRAへの移行が必要。
triage.notes: WHO・ECDCによる国際的監視下にあり、接触者追跡の達成率（79.7%）が目標95%を下回る等、対応能力の限界が示唆される。北キブ、イツリ等複数州にまたがる大規模流行で、コミュニティでの死亡が治療センターでの死亡を上回っており、感染制御・ケア体制の課題が深刻。

article.articleHeadline: UAE eases Ebola-related entry measures for Ugandans
article.articleSummary: UAE eases Ebola-related entry measures for Ugandan nationals as of 11 November 2026. The NCEMA, MoHAP, and ICP announced that precautionary measures introduced in June 2026 due to Ebola developments are being eased. Ugandan nationals may enter with new UAE visas provided at least 21 days have passed since departure from Uganda. Ugandan students who were enrolled in UAE institutions before June 2026 may enter with family members, under approved health procedures. Other categories include administrative staff at the Ugandan Embassy in the UAE with ordinary passports and their families, and holders of Ugandan diplomatic and special passports, per approved procedures. Humanitarian and medical cases will be assessed individually in coordination with authorities. Medical travel requires approved reports detailing diagnosis, treatment facility, and start date. Measures for the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the Republic of South Sudan remain in effect.

triage.headline_ja: UAE、ウガンダ人に対するエボラ関連入国措置を緩和
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱に関連し、UAEがウガンダ人への入国制限を緩和する一方、DRC・南スーダンへの渡航制限措置は継続中であり、IHR基準（深刻性・国際的拡大・渡航制限）に複数該当する。
triage.notes: 記事の主眼はUAEの入国規制緩和（ウガンダ人対象）だが、DRCおよび南スーダンに対する渡航制限は継続中とされ、エボラ流行の継続を示唆する内容。ウガンダ・スーダンは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。DRCのみ対象国として該当。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola, în Congo: peste 11.000 de cazuri și 5.387 de decese. Cea mai gravă epidemie din istoria țării
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in Congo: over 11,000 cases and 5,387 deaths. The deadliest epidemic in the country's history.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has 11,042 confirmed cases and at least 5,387 deaths as of November 10, 2026. The Bundibugyo strain drives what authorities call the deadliest Ebola epidemic in the country's history and the second-largest on record after 2014–2016 West Africa. Eight of 26 provinces are affected, with numerous deaths outside treatment centers. Delayed case detection, ongoing armed conflict, and an overwhelmed health system hinder outbreak control. There is no vaccine or treatment specific to Bundibugyo, and the case fatality rate is about 50%. The virus now spans East, Central, and West Africa, representing the broadest geographic spread to date. The WHO has approved clinical testing of two Ebola vaccines, with results expected in early 2027, potentially expanding tools to curb transmission.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでエボラ出血熱：感染者1万1000人超、死者5387人。同国史上最悪の流行
triage.triage_reason: DRCで11,042症例・5,387人死亡（致死率約50%）という同国史上最大規模のエボラ流行が進行中で、武力紛争・医療崩壊により制御困難、地理的拡大も見られるためフルRRAへ進むべき案件。
triage.notes: Bluedotの発生地域にモザンビーク・アンゴラが含まれるが、記事サマリーではDRC国内の流行のみが主題であり、対象国リストにも含まれないため除外した。

article.articleHeadline: Kenia dio de alta a su último paciente con ébola, comenzando la cuenta regresiva de 42 días.
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Kenya discharged its last Ebola patient, beginning the 42-day countdown.
article.articleSummary: Kenya discharged its last Ebola patient on November 11, 2026, initiating a 42-day countdown to an Ebola-free declaration on December 23 if no new infections occur; Health Minister Aden Duale calls it twice the longest incubation. Congo reports 11,042 infections and 5,387 deaths, with regional cases over 11,000 since May. The index patient traveled from Congo into Kenya via Uganda, transmitting Ebola to four relatives and four health workers; he and his mother died, seven others recovered, and 135 contacts were identified. Kenya says all confirmed cases tie to the index case, with no community transmission. Saudi Arabia suspended visas Oct 30, affecting Kenyans headed to the Gulf. Kenya maintains enhanced airport screening, a dedicated gate for arrivals from 10 at-risk countries, an Ebola hotline, and five isolation facilities with 241 beds. The outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo Ebola virus, for which no vaccine or treatment exists; care is symptom-based.

triage.headline_ja: ケニアが最後のエボラ患者を退院させ、42日間のカウントダウンを開始
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ発のエボラ出血熱がケニアに越境伝播し、死者5,387人・感染11,042人规模の地域流行となっており、サウジアラビアによる渡航制限も発生しているためIHR基準4つ全てに該当する。
triage.notes: 記事はコンゴ発生源のエボラ流行がケニア・ウガンダ経由で越境伝播した事例を扱うが、対象国リストにはコンゴのみ該当。ケニア・ウガンダ・サウジアラビアは対象国リスト外のためverified_locationsから除外。コンゴでの感染拡大が依然として続いている点から地域全体のリスク評価が必要と考えられる。

article.articleHeadline: T7News | Casos de Covid-19 sobem 290% em São José dos Campos e ligam sinal de alerta no Vale do Paraíba
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: T7News | COVID-19 cases rise 290% in São José dos Campos and trigger a warning signal in Paraíba Valley.
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 is rising again in the Vale do Paraíba, led by São José dos Campos. From September to October 2026, confirmed cases jumped from 21 to 82 (a 290% increase), and test positivity rose from 3.42% to 13.5%. No COVID-19 deaths were reported in São José dos Campos during the period. Fiocruz notes higher numbers of severe COVID-19 cases and hospitalizations for Severe Acute Respiratory Illness (SARI), known as SRAG in Brazilian reporting, across five states including São Paulo. Co-circulating respiratory viruses such as rhinovirus and metapneumovirus are present. Authorities emphasize that indicators remain below worst-pandemic levels but urge vaccination updates, especially for the elderly, immunocompromised, and those with comorbidities in the Paraíba Valley.

article.articleHeadline: Quais são os sintomas da variante de covid-19 que está em alta no Brasil
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: What are the symptoms of the COVID-19 variant that is on the rise in Brazil?
article.articleSummary: Variant XFG, aka Stratus, dominates SARS-CoV-2 lineages in Brazil in 2026, about 90% of samples through week 43, descending from Omicron. No evidence XFG causes more severe disease, hospitalizations, or deaths; vaccines protect against severe outcomes. WHO classifies XFG as a Variant Under Monitoring (VUM). Genomic surveillance shows a rise in COVID-19 cases across 18 states, including São Paulo, Bahia, Minas Gerais, and Santa Catarina, though all remain at low risk. From year start to week 43, Brazil recorded 118,851 influenza-like illnesses; 2,199 sequences identified 127 lineages, with XFG and descendants about 90%. JN.1, an Omicron subvariant, was detected. XFG symptoms include sore throat, hoarseness, dry cough, nasal congestion, fever (usually mild), fatigue, and headaches. A small uptick in severe cases is noted in Mato Grosso, Rio de Janeiro, São Paulo, and Santa Catarina, but incidence remains low. More than 7.4 million vaccine doses have been administered this year.

triage.headline_ja: ブラジルで増加中のCOVID-19変異株の症状とは
triage.triage_reason: XFG(Stratus)変異株はWHOによりVUM指定されているが重症化や死亡の増加は確認されておらず、リスクは低いとされているため、フルRRAではなく経過観察が妥当。
triage.notes: WHOはXFGをVariant Under Monitoring(VUM)に分類しており、重症度増加の証拠はないが、18州で症例増加傾向があるため動向注視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola cases cross 11,000 in DR Congo as deaths exceed 5,300
article.articleSummary: DR Congo's Ebola outbreak, driven by the rare Bundibugyo strain, has surpassed 11,000 confirmed cases and 5,387 deaths as of 2026-11-11. It is the country's largest and deadliest Ebola outbreak, with eight of the 26 provinces affected. Containment has been hindered by delayed detection, armed conflict, and overwhelmed health systems. The outbreak ranks as the second-largest and deadliest Ebola event on record globally, behind the 2014–2016 West Africa outbreak, which produced almost 28,600 cases and 11,000 deaths. Kinshasa-based government data underscore the scale and ongoing challenge to curb transmission across affected provinces.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ感染者数が11,000人を超え、死者数が5,300人を超える
triage.triage_reason: 死亡率の高いエボラ出血熱が過去最大規模で拡大し、8州に及び、紛争により封じ込めが困難な状況で、IHR基準・WPRO基準の双方で複数該当する重大な公衆衛生上の緊急事態。
triage.notes: 史上2番目に大きく致死性の高いエボラ流行であり、武力紛争下での対応困難さが指摘されている。アンゴラは発生地域として付与されているが記事本文中に具体的言及がないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: 刚果（金）埃博拉疫情确诊病例突破1.1万例 死亡人数超过5300人
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo surpasses 11,000 confirmed cases; death toll exceeds 5,300.
article.articleSummary: An outbreak of Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 11,000 laboratory-confirmed cases, with deaths exceeding 5,300. The epicenter is eastern DRC, mainly Ituri Province and North Kivu Province, with Ituri accounting for about 70% of cases; North Kivu is a newly important transmission area. Ongoing conflict, weak health systems, and high population movement hinder control efforts. Attacks on healthcare workers and community distrust impede surveillance, testing, and contact tracing. The outbreak has spilled over into Uganda, Kenya, and Nigeria via cross-border transmission. WHO and national agencies are scaling up surveillance, contact tracing, and logistics, but no approved specific vaccine or therapy exists for Bundibugyo virus. Priorities: secure access for medical teams, rapid isolation, and community outreach; this is the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record after 2014–2016 West Africa.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱、確認症例が11,000例を突破、死者5,300人超

article.articleHeadline: Kenia entließ seinen letzten Ebola-Patienten, Beginn des 42-tägigen Countdowns.
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Kenya discharged its last Ebola patient, marking the start of the 42-day countdown.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in Congo (Bundibugyo strain) has caused 11,042 infections and 5,387 deaths as of 11 November, with the May start spreading to Uganda and Nigeria via travelers. The first patient traveled from Congo through Uganda to Kenya, transmitting to four family members and four health workers; the patient and mother died, while seven others recovered. Officially 135 contacts were identified, and all confirmed cases were linked to the first patient’s contact list, with no community transmission. Kenya discharged its last Ebola patient on 11 November, beginning a 42‑day countdown to being declared Ebola‑free on 23 December if no new infections occur; preventive measures will continue. Kenya operates an airport gate for travelers from 10 at‑risk countries, conducts thermal screening, requires health declarations, and runs an Ebola hotline and five facilities with 241 isolation beds. The Bundibugyo strain has no vaccine or treatment; care is symptomatic. Saudi Arabia’s 30 October visa suspension for Kenyan workers was urged to be reconsidered given the imported case.

article.articleHeadline: Έμπολα: Περισσότερα από 11.000 κρούσματα έχουν καταγραφεί στη ΛΔ Κονγκό | AlphaTV
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola: More than 11,000 cases have been recorded in the Democratic Republic of the Congo | AlphaTV.
article.articleSummary: 11,042 Ebola infections and 5,387 deaths (about 48.8% case fatality) with roughly 2,990 recoveries in the Democratic Republic of Congo as of 11 November 2026, marking the 17th outbreak in the country. Originating in Ituri province in the northeast, the outbreak has spread to seven additional provinces, with Ituri and North Kivu as the epicenters; cross-border cases have been detected in Uganda, Kenya and Nigeria. Response is hampered by ongoing conflict and attacks on health facilities, including a center in the Lolwa/Lolua community, and clashes in Fataki; Allied Democratic Forces insurgents are active in Ituri, Upper Uele, and North Kivu. No licensed vaccine for the Bundibugyo ebolavirus strain; Doctors Without Borders urges broader use of Ervebo (Zaire ebolavirus vaccine) and WHO is conducting a trial for cross-protection. In Kenya, nine cases since October, last patient discharged, with a 42-day countdown to end; 21-day quarantine for travelers from the DRC, and no new cases since October 19.

article.articleHeadline: Epidemia de ébola en RDC se convierte en la segunda más mortífera de la historia
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in the DRC becomes the second deadliest in history.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is the second deadliest in history, with over 11,000 confirmed cases and 5,387 deaths as of November 9, 2026, according to INSP. Case fatality 48.8%. About 2,990 recoveries; 651 still hospitalized or in isolation. Ituri province (epicenter) accounts for 57.7% of new cases on Nov 9, followed by North Kivu with 32.7%. This is the 17th Ebola outbreak in the DRC. The strain is Bundibugyo, for which no targeted treatment exists. WHO is testing two vaccines in Phase 1 trials and has reported positive safety signals. The outbreak has spread across borders to Uganda, Kenya, and Nigeria. Uganda declared the outbreak over on August 26 after 20 infections and 2 deaths. Europe has reported linked cases, with France testing one infection; four people evacuated from DRC to the Netherlands, Germany, and the United Kingdom after infection.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱流行、史上2番目の致死的な流行に

article.articleHeadline: Varginha confirma 24 casos de escabiose em cinco escolas da cidade
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Varginha confirms 24 cases of scabies in five of the city's schools.
article.articleSummary: Varginha, Brazil reports 24 confirmed cases of scabies (Sarcoptes scabiei) across five municipal schools, triggering intensified epidemiological surveillance and control measures. Cases were mapped through November 10, with daily monitoring and a weekly epidemiological bulletin to be published on the official portal semus.varginha.mg.gov.br. Scabies spreads mainly via prolonged direct skin contact and via shared towels, clothes, or bed linens; predominant symptoms are intense nocturnal itching and skin lesions. In response, the Municipal Health Secretariat has strengthened prevention and case management since late October, including an instruction note to schools and November technical meetings with Health and Education to standardize care pathways and isolate suspected cases in both public and private institutions. Public guidance emphasizes not sharing personal items, proper cleaning of clothing, seeking medical care if symptoms appear, and following the prescribed treatment for contacts. The bulletin will be updated weekly or as needed.

triage.notes: 疥癬はブラジルで発生しているが対象国リストにブラジルは含まれるものの、公衆衛生上の重大性が低く、局地的な学校内アウトブレイクであるため、対象国リストに該当があってもDISMISS判定とした。地元保健当局が通常の監視・対応を実施中。

article.articleHeadline: Mpox: o que você deve saber sobre essa doença que está crescendo no Brasil
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Mpox: What You Should Know About This Disease That Is Growing in Brazil
article.articleSummary: As of 11 November 2026, mpox (monkeypox) cases are rising in Brazil, concentrated in four states: Rio de Janeiro, São Paulo, Ceará, and the Federal District. Most infections are mild or moderate; some are severe. Symptoms include skin eruptions and lesions, swollen lymph nodes, fever, headache, body aches, chills, and weakness. Transmission is mainly via direct contact with infected people or contaminated items, including lesion secretions and bodily fluids such as pus, blood, and saliva, as well as objects like clothing, towels, sheets, and utensils. There is no specific approved mpox medicine; treatment is supportive, and most cases recover within two to four weeks. Vaccination is recommended in Brazil only for certain groups, notably people living with HIV/AIDS, PrEP users, and laboratory professionals handling mpox samples. Preventive measures: avoid contact with suspected/confirmed cases, do not share personal items, wash hands, disinfect surfaces, and seek care after exposure.

triage.headline_ja: Mpox:ブラジルで増加しているこの病気について知っておくべきこと
triage.triage_reason: ブラジル国内でMpox症例が増加しているが、具体的な症例数・死亡数・国際拡大の兆候等の詳細情報が不足しており、続報を注視する必要がある。
triage.notes: Mpoxは既知の疾患であり、ブラジル国内の複数州（リオデジャネイロ、サンパウロ、セアラ、連邦直轄区）で症例増加が報告されているが、具体的な数値データがなく評価には限界がある。
